definition_zh: 生物化学；生物体的化学过程与化学组成
definition_en: the science of the chemical processes and substances of living organisms
core_image: 把一只活细胞拆成一张分子反应清单
scene: 两份血检报告摊在桌上，钾的数值低得显眼。Her biochemistry results showed low potassium after two weeks of illness.
sceneCN: 这里 biochemistry 指「生化检验结果」（第 8 个义项：一组血液化学指标）；句意：患病两周后，她的生化结果显示血钾偏低。

pos.zh: 生物化学；生物体的化学过程；生化检验指标（作不可数名词，指学科或过程时一般不加 -s）

senses.title: The discipline
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies the chemical processes and substances of living organisms
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物体内化学过程与化学物质的学科
senses.example: Biochemistry sits between biology and chemistry on the university campus.
senses.exampleCN: 在大学里，生物化学处在生物学与化学之间。
senses.why: The suffix -istry names a field of study, so the compound first of all labels a discipline with two parent sciences.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -istry 表示研究领域，因此这个词首先命名一门由两门母科学交叉而成的学科。

senses.title: The processes in a body
senses.definition: the chemical processes that take place in a living organism
senses.definitionCN: 活生物体内发生的化学过程
senses.example: The biochemistry of the insect changes sharply when it enters hibernation.
senses.exampleCN: 这种昆虫进入休眠时，其体内的化学过程会发生剧烈变化。
senses.why: The same noun can name not only the study but also its object, because a science and the processes it studies are habitually spoken of with one word.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既可以是学科，也可以是研究对象，因为人们习惯用一个词同时指「学问」和「这门学问所研究的那些过程」。

senses.title: Chemical makeup
senses.definition: the chemical composition of a tissue, organism or substance
senses.definitionCN: 某组织、生物或物质的化学组成
senses.example: The biochemistry of the seed oil makes it suitable for cold climates.
senses.exampleCN: 这种种子油的化学组成使它适合寒冷气候。
senses.why: If processes are the verbs of a cell, the substances are its nouns; the word extends naturally from what happens to what is there.
senses.whyCN: 如果化学过程是细胞里的动词，那么化学物质就是名词；词义从「发生什么」自然延伸到「有什么」。

senses.title: A course or subject
senses.definition: a course, textbook or examination subject dealing with the chemistry of life
senses.definitionCN: 讲授生命化学的课程、教材或考试科目
senses.example: Biochemistry is a required course for medical students here.
senses.exampleCN: 生物化学是这里医学生的必修课。
senses.why: Academic institutions name subjects after the discipline, so the word also labels the thing taught and examined.
senses.whyCN: 学术机构用学科名来命名科目，于是这个词也指被讲授、被考试的那门课。

senses.title: Department or laboratory
senses.titleCN: 生物化学系；生化实验室
senses.definition: an academic department or research unit devoted to the subject
senses.definitionCN: 从事该学科的系或研究单位
senses.example: The biochemistry at this hospital runs the newborn screening programme.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院的生化科负责新生儿筛查项目。
senses.why: A metonymy turns the discipline into the place and the staff that practise it, a pattern common to names of departments.
senses.whyCN: 这是一种转喻：用学科名指从事该学科的场所与人员，院系名称普遍采用这种说法。

senses.title: Clinical branch
senses.definition: the branch that measures chemical substances in patients' samples to diagnose and monitor disease
senses.definitionCN: 测定患者样本中的化学物质以诊断和监测疾病的分支
senses.example: Clinical biochemistry detected the salt imbalance before symptoms appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 临床生物化学在症状出现前就检出了盐类失衡。
senses.why: Medicine split off a service-oriented branch, and the parent word now covers both the pure science and its hospital application.
senses.whyCN: 医学分出一个面向服务的分支，母词于是同时涵盖纯科学与医院里的应用。

senses.title: Chemistry of a pathway
senses.titleCN: 某条代谢通路的生化机制
senses.definition: the specific reactions and molecules of one metabolic route
senses.definitionCN: 某一代谢通路的具体反应与分子
senses.example: The biochemistry of fat storage explains why the liver enlarges.
senses.exampleCN: 脂肪储存的生化机制解释了肝脏为何增大。
senses.why: With of plus a named process, the noun narrows to the chemistry that belongs to that process alone.
senses.whyCN: 当它与表示某个具体过程的词组成介词短语连用时，这个名词就收窄为「该过程专属的那套化学」。

senses.title: Laboratory results
senses.definition: in clinical speech, the set of chemical measurements reported for a patient
senses.definitionCN: 临床上指为患者报告的一组化学测定结果
senses.example: Her biochemistry was normal apart from a low bicarbonate level.
senses.exampleCN: 除碳酸氢盐偏低外，她的生化指标都正常。
senses.why: Doctors compress 'the results of the biochemistry test' into the single word, another metonymy from discipline to output.
senses.whyCN: 医生把「生化检验的结果」压缩成一个词，这是又一次转喻：从学科名转向它的产出。

senses.title: Figurative inner workings
senses.definition: the hidden chemical or emotional workings of something, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某事物隐藏的化学或情感机制
senses.example: Popular science writes about the biochemistry of attraction.
senses.exampleCN: 科普写作会谈论吸引力的生化机制。
senses.why: Once the word means 'the chemistry behind a phenomenon', it can be borrowed for any hidden mechanism, especially in popular writing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「现象背后的化学」，它就能被借去指任何隐藏机制，在通俗写作中尤其常见。

intro.en: Biochemistry is a 19th-century compound of a Greek prefix for life and an English noun for chemistry, coined as the two sciences converged.
intro.cn: biochemistry 是 19 世纪的复合词，由表示生命的希腊语前缀与表示化学的英语名词构成，诞生于两门科学交汇之时。

items.en: bio- comes from Greek bios, 'life, course of life'. It became a scientific prefix in the 19th century, first in biology and then in a swarm of compounds.
items.cn: bio- 出自希腊语 bios「生命、生命历程」。它在 19 世纪成为科学前缀，先用于 biology，随后进入一大批复合词。

items.en: Chemistry reached English through alchemy, Medieval Latin alchimia and Arabic al-kimiya, usually traced to Greek khemeia. The earliest origin remains disputed, so the deeper etymology is uncertain.
items.cn: chemistry 经 alchemy、中世纪拉丁语 alchimia、阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 进入英语，通常追溯到希腊语 khemeia。更早的来源仍有争议，深层词源属于来源不确定。

items.en: The compound biochemistry is generally dated to the middle decades of the 19th century, when physiologists began to describe life in chemical terms. The exact coinage is not settled.
items.cn: biochemistry 这一复合词一般认为出现在 19 世纪中叶，当时生理学家开始用化学语言描述生命。确切的首创者尚无定论。

items.en: Around 1900 the field acquired its modern shape as enzymes, proteins and metabolic pathways were worked out, and university chairs followed.
items.cn: 约 1900 年，随着酶、蛋白质与代谢通路被阐明，这门学科获得现代形态，大学教席也随之设立。

items.en: In the 20th century hospitals created clinical biochemistry laboratories, adding the everyday sense of a set of test results.
items.cn: 20 世纪医院设立临床生化实验室，由此增加了「一组检验结果」这一日常义。

items.en: After the 1950s, biochemistry merged with molecular biology, and the word now covers both the classic chemistry of life and its molecular successor.
items.cn: 1950 年代以后，生物化学与分子生物学融合，这个词如今同时涵盖经典的生命化学与其分子层面的后继者。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective and from neighbouring life-science words; the second separates it from words for adjacent levels of study.
note.cn: 第一组把这个名词与它的形容词以及与相邻的生命科学词分开；第二组把它与邻近研究层次的词分开。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of the chemistry of life'; it describes tests, pathways and substances, while biochemistry names the field or the processes.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「生命化学的」，用来修饰检验、通路、物质；biochemistry 则指学科或过程。

entries.definition: The study of living things in general, including their structure, growth and behaviour; it is wider than biochemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指研究生物及其结构、生长与行为的学科，范围比生物化学更宽。

entries.definition: The person who practises biochemistry; the field itself never takes the -ist ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事生物化学的人；学科本身不能加 -ist 词尾。

entries.definition: The study of biological processes at the level of DNA, RNA and proteins; it overlaps heavily with biochemistry but centres on information flow.
entries.definitionCN: 在 DNA、RNA 与蛋白质层面研究生命过程，与生物化学高度重叠，但更侧重信息传递。

entries.definition: The study of how organs and tissues function; it asks what a body does, while biochemistry asks what reactions make it possible.
entries.definitionCN: 研究器官与组织如何运作，关心「身体做什么」；生物化学关心「哪些反应使之成为可能」。

entries.definition: The science of substances and their reactions in general; biochemistry is its living subset.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质及其反应的一般科学；生物化学是它在生命领域的子集。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + chemistry: the chemistry of life.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ chemistry「化学」：生命的化学。

normal.en: The family runs biochemical, biochemist, biomolecule and metabolite.
normal.cn: 同族词有 biochemical、biochemist、biomolecule、metabolite。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: clinical biochemistry, biochemistry department, plant biochemistry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：临床生物化学、生物化学系、植物生物化学。

normal.en: Hospitals say 'her biochemistry is normal' when they mean the lab panel.
normal.cn: 医院说「她的生化正常」，指的是一组化验指标。

normal.en: The word names both the field and the thing the field studies, like 'history' naming both a discipline and a past.
normal.cn: 这个词既指学科，也指学科研究的对象，就像 history 既指历史学也指过去。

abstract.en: Think of a city's traffic map: biochemistry is the map of every chemical route inside a cell.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市交通图：生物化学就是细胞内每条化学反应路线的地图。

abstract.en: A biochemistry panel is a weather report for the body's internal climate.
abstract.cn: 一组生化指标就像身体内部气候的天气预报。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every tool is a molecule and every worker is an enzyme.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊：每件工具都是分子，每个工人都是酶。

examples.en: Biochemistry explains how cells extract energy from sugar.
examples.cn: 生物化学解释了细胞如何从糖中获取能量。

examples.en: She chose biochemistry because she wanted to understand life at the molecular level.
examples.cn: 她选择生物化学，是因为想在分子层面理解生命。

examples.en: The hospital's biochemistry laboratory reports results within an hour.
examples.cn: 医院的生化实验室一小时内出结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bio（生命）+ chemistry（化学）」→ 研究生命里的化学 → 生物化学

root: 希腊语 bios「生命」+ chemistry（经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya、中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 上溯至希腊语 khemeia「冶金术」），19 世纪合成为 biochemistry。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the discipline to its object, then to its composition, its teaching, its institutions, its clinical branch, its results and finally to figurative inner workings.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从学科移向研究对象，再到化学组成、课程、机构、临床分支、检验结果，最后落到比喻性的内在机制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list of molecular reactions extracted from a living cell.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一只活细胞里抽出来的一张分子反应清单。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND ITS OBJECT: the field itself, and the processes it studies.
branches.cn: 学科与其对象：这门学问本身，以及它所研究的那些过程。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE: what the cell contains rather than what it does.
branches.cn: 物质：细胞里有什么，而不是它做了什么。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: the subject as taught, and the department or laboratory that practises it.
branches.cn: 机构：作为科目的课程，以及从事该学科的院系或实验室。

branches.en: SPECIALISED ROUTES: a clinical branch and the chemistry of one named pathway.
branches.cn: 专门路线：一个临床分支，以及某条被点名的通路的化学。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND METAPHOR: the reported results, and the hidden chemistry of any phenomenon.
branches.cn: 产出与比喻：报告出来的结果，以及任何现象背后隐藏的化学。

intro.en: Biochemistry is a two-root compound with a Greek prefix and an English noun, plus the abstract suffix -istry.
intro.cn: biochemistry 是双词根复合词：希腊语前缀加英语名词，再带抽象名词后缀 -istry。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies the element for life; the chemistry element came through Arabic and Medieval Latin. The suffix -istry descends from Latin -ia and Greek -ia.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供表示生命的成分；表示化学的成分经阿拉伯语与中世纪拉丁语传入；后缀 -istry 源自拉丁语 -ia 与希腊语 -ia。

items.example: Biochemistry became a separate degree in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 生物化学在 20 世纪成为独立学位。

items.meaning: relating to the chemistry of life
items.example: The biochemical assay took two hours.
items.exampleCN: 这项生化测定用了两小时。

items.meaning: one who studies the chemistry of life
items.example: The biochemist grew crystals of the enzyme.
items.exampleCN: 这位生物化学家培养了该酶的晶体。

items.example: Biology and biochemistry share their first element.
items.exampleCN: 生物学与生物化学共享第一个构词成分。

items.meaning: a molecule produced by or belonging to life
items.meaningCN: 由生命产生或属于生命的分子
items.example: Proteins are the most versatile biomolecules.
items.exampleCN: 蛋白质是最多才多艺的生物分子。

items.example: The drug's main metabolite is inactive.
items.exampleCN: 该药物的主要代谢产物没有活性。

items.meaning: a protein that catalyses a reaction
items.example: Each step of the pathway needs its own enzyme.
items.exampleCN: 通路的每一步都需要各自的酶。

items.meaning: the science of substances and reactions
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与反应的科学
items.example: Chemistry provides the methods biochemistry uses.
items.exampleCN: 化学提供了生物化学所用的方法。

items.meaning: relating to the treatment of patients
items.exampleCN: 临床生物化学报告血钾水平。

definition_zh: 可生物降解的；能被微生物分解的
definition_en: able to be broken down by living organisms, especially microorganisms, into simple natural substances
core_image: 一只纸盒埋在湿土里，边缘被菌丝啃成缺口，半年后只剩几片碎屑与深色的土
scene: 公园把塑料餐盒换成纸浆做的盒子，埋进堆肥坑里几个月后就只剩碎屑。The coffee shop now serves its meals in biodegradable trays.
sceneCN: 这里指材料能被微生物分解成简单天然物质（第 1 个义项：可被生物分解）；句意为这家咖啡馆现在用可生物降解的餐盘盛饭。

pos.zh: 可生物降解的；能被微生物分解的

derivatives.zh: 由表示「生命」的成分加表示「降级、分解」的动词构成，义为「生物降解」
由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「生物降解过程」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「可生物降解性」
该词去掉表示「生命」的成分后剩下的形容词，义为「可降解的」，降解方式不限
由表示否定的前缀加该词构成，义为「不可生物降解的」
相邻术语，指可在堆肥条件下分解并产出可用堆肥，义为「可堆肥的」

senses.title: Breakable down by living organisms
senses.definition: able to be decomposed by bacteria, fungi or other organisms rather than only by heat, light or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 能被细菌、真菌或其他生物分解，而不是只能靠热、光或化学品分解
senses.example: The liner is biodegradable, so it breaks down in soil within a season.
senses.exampleCN: 这种衬垫是可生物降解的，因此在一个季节内就能在土壤里分解。
senses.why: The first element means life and the last means able to be, so the word says living things can take it apart.
senses.whyCN: 前一个成分意为「生命」，后一个成分意为「能够被……」，因此这个词说的是活物能把它拆开。

senses.title: Leaving only harmless natural products
senses.titleCN: 分解后只留下无害的天然物质
senses.definition: breaking down into water, carbon dioxide, biomass and simple minerals rather than toxic residue
senses.definitionCN: 分解为水、二氧化碳、生物质与简单矿物质，而不是留下有毒残留
senses.example: A material is only fully biodegradable if no harmful residue is left behind.
senses.exampleCN: 一种材料只有不留下有害残留，才算完全可生物降解。
senses.why: Complete breakdown is judged by what remains, which is why the claim is tested rather than assumed.
senses.whyCN: 完全分解要看剩下什么来判断，这正是这一说法需要检测而不能想当然的原因。

senses.title: Dependent on specific conditions
senses.definition: requiring the right microbes, moisture, oxygen and temperature before decomposition can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 需要合适的微生物、湿度、氧气与温度，分解才能进行
senses.example: The bag is biodegradable but needs a warm, moist compost heap to break down at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这种袋子可生物降解，但必须有温暖潮湿的堆肥堆才能真正分解。
senses.why: Microbes are living workers, so their working conditions become conditions of the material.
senses.whyCN: 微生物是活着的工人，因此它们的工作条件就成了这种材料的条件。

senses.title: A property of packaging and products
senses.titleCN: 包装与制品的一项属性
senses.definition: a stated property of films, trays, bags, cutlery and detergents sold as environmentally preferable
senses.definitionCN: 薄膜、托盘、袋子、餐具与洗涤剂等被宣称为更环保产品时标明的属性
senses.example: The shop prints biodegradable on the box, but not the conditions needed.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在盒子上印了「可生物降解」，却没有印所需的分解条件。
senses.why: The word became a marketing attribute once disposable goods needed an environmental defence.
senses.whyCN: 一次性用品需要环境方面的辩护时，这个词就成了一种营销属性。

senses.title: Compostable as a stricter claim
senses.titleCN: 可堆肥：更严格的一类声称
senses.definition: able to break down in a defined composting system within a set time and leave usable compost
senses.definitionCN: 能在规定的堆肥系统内于限定时间内分解，并留下可用的堆肥
senses.example: The fork is compostable at industrial temperatures but not biodegradable in a garden heap.
senses.exampleCN: 这把叉子能在工业温度下堆肥分解，在花园堆肥堆里却不能生物降解。
senses.why: Composting adds a time limit and a quality test, so it is the narrower and better-evidenced claim.
senses.whyCN: 堆肥增加了时间限制与质量检验，因此是更窄、证据更充分的说法。

senses.title: Distinct from merely degradable
senses.definition: differing from degradable, which covers breakdown by light, heat or mechanical action as well as microbes
senses.definitionCN: 与「可降解」不同，后者把光、热或机械作用造成的分解也计算在内
senses.example: A photodegradable sheet fragments in sunlight yet is not biodegradable.
senses.exampleCN: 一种光降解薄膜在阳光下会碎裂，却不是可生物降解的。
senses.why: Fragmenting is not decomposing, and the word keeps that distinction by naming the living agent.
senses.whyCN: 碎裂不等于分解，这个词通过点明「生物」这一作用者来守住这条界线。

senses.title: A certification and label claim
senses.definition: a claim checked against a published standard before it may appear on a product
senses.definitionCN: 须按已发布标准检验后才能出现在产品上的声称
senses.example: Only two of the nine bags carried a certified biodegradable mark.
senses.exampleCN: 九种袋子中只有两种带有经认证的可生物降解标志。
senses.why: Because the word sells, it needed standards to stop it from meaning nothing.
senses.whyCN: 正因为这个词能卖货，才需要标准来防止它变得毫无意义。

senses.title: Limited in a landfill
senses.definition: decomposing very slowly or not at all when buried without oxygen in a sealed landfill
senses.definitionCN: 在缺氧的封闭填埋场中被埋时分解极慢，甚至完全不分解
senses.example: Buried without air, even a biodegradable cup may release methane for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 在无氧条件下被埋，即使可生物降解的杯子也可能数十年持续释放甲烷。
senses.why: The adjective describes a capacity, not a guarantee, and the missing conditions explain the gap.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述一种能力，而不是一项保证，缺失的条件正好解释了这一落差。

senses.title: A timescale rather than an instant
senses.definition: breaking down over months or years, with the duration depending on material and setting
senses.definitionCN: 在数月或数年尺度上分解，时长取决于材料与所处环境
senses.example: The manufacturer states that the tray is biodegradable within ninety days in commercial compost.
senses.exampleCN: 制造商说明这种托盘在商业堆肥条件下九十天内可生物降解。
senses.why: Living decomposition is slow by nature, so any label for it has to carry a period.
senses.whyCN: 生物分解天生缓慢，因此任何相关标注都必须带上一个时间。

intro.en: The word is a twentieth-century compound. A Greek element for life is joined to a Latin verb for stepping down, and an English adjective ending completes it.
intro.cn: 这个词是二十世纪复合词：希腊语的「生命」成分接上拉丁语表示「逐级下降」的动词，再由英语形容词词尾收尾。

items.en: Bios meant life, and it became the standard first element in compounds about living processes.
items.cn: 这个词意为生命，后来成了表示生命过程的复合词的标准前项。

items.en: Gradus meant a step, and it supplied the image of moving down one level at a time.
items.cn: 这个词意为一步、一级，提供了「一级一级往下走」的形象。

items.en: The verb meant to lower in rank, built from the prefix for down and the noun for step.
items.cn: 这个动词意为降低等级，由表示「向下」的前缀与表示「级」的名词构成。

items.en: French carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century, first as a word about rank and later about condition.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词带入英语，时在十四世纪，先指等级，后指状态。

items.en: The ending meant able to be, and it turned the verb into a capacity rather than an event.
items.cn: 这个词尾意为「能够被……」，把动词变成一种能力而非一次事件。

items.en: Chemists and packaging engineers formed the compound in the mid-twentieth century; its exact first appearance is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 化学家与包装工程师在二十世纪中叶造出这个复合词；其确切首见时间只能给约数。

note.en: The first group shares the life or step element; the second group names other ways materials break down.
note.cn: 第一组共用「生命」或「级」的成分；第二组是材料分解的其他方式。

entries.definition: The verb for being broken down by living organisms.
The process itself, as studied and measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指被研究与测量的分解过程本身。

entries.definition: The property of being able to decompose biologically.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被生物分解的性质。

entries.definition: Able to break down by any means, including light and heat.
entries.definitionCN: 指能通过任何方式分解，包括光与热。

entries.definition: Variety of life; it shares the life element but belongs to the variety stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指生命多样性；共用「生命」成分，但属于「多样」词干。

entries.definition: Able to break down in a composting system within a stated time and leave usable compost.
entries.definitionCN: 指能在堆肥系统内于规定时间分解并留下可用堆肥。

entries.definition: Able to be broken down into simpler parts, without saying by what.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被分解成更简单的部分，但不说由什么分解。

entries.definition: Broken down by light, which may leave fragments rather than simple substances.
entries.definitionCN: 指由光分解，可能留下碎片而非简单物质。

entries.definition: Able to be processed into new material, a different route from decomposition.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被加工成新材料，是与分解不同的一条路径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations take the word apart into life, step and capacity, then put it back into a compost heap.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把词拆成「生命」「级」与「能力」，再把它放回堆肥堆里。

normal.en: Bio is life, degrade is stepping down, and able says it can be done: life can step it down.
normal.cn: 前项是生命，动词是逐级下降，词尾是「能够」：活物能把它降下来。

normal.en: Biodegrade and biodegradation are the verb and the process; the adjective ends in a different suffix.
normal.cn: 动词与过程各有其词形，形容词的词尾又不同。

normal.en: Compostable is the stronger claim, because it adds a time limit and a quality test.
normal.cn: 「可堆肥」是更强的说法，因为它加了时限与质量检验。

normal.en: A sealed landfill has no oxygen, so even a degradable cup may last for decades.
normal.cn: 封闭填埋场没有氧气，所以即使可降解杯子也可能存留数十年。

normal.en: The label should carry a period, because biological breakdown is measured in months, not minutes.
normal.cn: 标签应当带时限，因为生物分解以月计，而不是以分钟计。

abstract.en: Biodegradable is a promise about the future made by a material that cannot keep it alone; it needs a place with the right microbes.
abstract.cn: 「可生物降解」是材料对未来作出的承诺，而它无法独自兑现，需要一个有合适微生物的地方。

abstract.en: Being edible to microbes is not the same as being harmless: what matters is what is left after the meal.
abstract.cn: 能被微生物吃掉不等于无害，关键是这顿饭吃完剩下什么。

abstract.en: Every claim of return to nature rests on a hidden set of conditions, and those conditions are the real subject.
abstract.cn: 每一种「回归自然」的说法都依赖一整套隐性条件，而那套条件才是真正的主题。

examples.en: The new mulch is fully biodegradable and breaks down within one season.
examples.cn: 这种新覆盖物完全可生物降解，一个季节内就会分解。

examples.en: Biodegradable bags still need oxygen to decompose, so they fail in sealed landfills.
examples.cn: 可生物降解袋子仍需氧气才能分解，因此在封闭填埋场里失效。

examples.en: The lab tested whether the film was biodegradable under soil conditions.
examples.cn: 实验室检测了这种薄膜在土壤条件下是否可生物降解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「拜欧迪格雷德波」——拜欧是生命，迪格雷德是降级，波是能够：生命能够把它降级拆开

root: 希腊语 bios「生命」+ 拉丁语 degradare「降低等级」← de-「向下」+ gradus「级、步」；英语经法语于十四世纪引入表示「降级」的动词，二十世纪中叶再加表示「能够被……」的词尾构成该形容词，确切首见时间只能给约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses separate what the word promises from what it requires: the living agent, the harmless residue, the conditions, the product, the stricter compost claim, the weaker degradable claim, certification, landfills and time.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把承诺与前提分开：分解者、无害残留、所需条件、产品属性、更严的堆肥声称、更宽的降解说法、认证、填埋场与时间尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper tray in damp soil, its edges eaten away by fungal threads into crumbs.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿土里的一只纸托盘，边缘被菌丝啃成碎屑。

branches.en: THE AGENT: bacteria and fungi do the work, not heat or light.
branches.cn: 作用者：干活的是细菌与真菌，而不是热或光。

branches.en: THE RESIDUE: what is left must be water, gas, biomass and minerals.
branches.cn: 残留：剩下必须是水、气体、生物质与矿物。

branches.en: THE CONDITIONS AND THE CLOCK: microbes need moisture, air and warmth, and the process runs in months or years.
branches.cn: 条件与时钟：微生物需要湿度、空气与温度，过程以月或年计。

branches.en: THE MARKET AND THE CHECK: a product attribute that must be certified before it sells.
branches.cn: 市场与检验：一种必须先经认证才能售卖的产品属性。

branches.en: THE NEIGHBOURING CLAIMS: a stricter compost standard on one side, a looser degradable one on the other.
branches.cn: 邻近声称：一边是更严的堆肥标准，一边是更宽的降解说法。

intro.en: Three elements make the word: a Greek life element, a Latin step verb and a Latin capacity ending.
intro.cn: 三个成分构成这个词：希腊语「生命」、拉丁语「逐级下降」动词与拉丁语「能够」词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies gradus, degradare and the ending -abilis, all recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「级」「降低等级」与词尾三种有记录的形式。

items.example: It names the agent that does the work.
It marks movement to a lower state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记向更低状态的移动。

items.example: It gives the sense of one level at a time.
items.exampleCN: 它给出「一级一级」的意思。

items.example: It turns an event into a capacity.
It is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是形容词背后的动词。

items.example: It marks material that microbes cannot use.
items.exampleCN: 它标记微生物用不了的材料。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词去掉词尾并还原为动词，义为「生物降解」
由该动词加过程名词词尾构成，义为「生物降解过程」
由该形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「可生物降解性」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不可生物降解的」

definition_zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平
definition_en: the variety of living organisms and the ecological systems they form, measured at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels
core_image: 同一片森林里，每一层都长着不同的生命
scene: 这座岛与大陆隔开千万年，物种因此自成一套。The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity, with species found nowhere else on Earth.
sceneCN: 这里 biodiversity 是「生物多样性」（第 1 个义项：一个地区的物种多样性）；句意：这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性，有些物种在地球上别处都找不到。场景要点：海岛、多层的热带植被、不同种类的鸟与昆虫、记录表、望远镜。

pos.zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平

collocations.zh: 生物多样性补偿（生态补偿机制）

derivatives.zh: 生物多样性极高的（用于 megadiverse countries）

senses.title: Species diversity in a place
senses.titleCN: 物种多样性：一个地区有多少种生物
senses.definition: the variety and number of species living in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区内物种的多样程度和数量
senses.example: The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性。
senses.why: bio- supplies 'life' and diversity supplies 'turned different ways'. The first sense counts how many kinds of living thing share a place: difference among organisms is the core of the word, and species are the easiest differences to see.
senses.whyCN: bio- 提供“生命”，diversity 提供“转向各方”。第一个义项数的是一个地方共享着多少种生物：生物之间的差异是这个词的核心，而物种是最容易看见的差异。

senses.title: Genetic diversity within a species
senses.titleCN: 遗传多样性：同一物种内部的基因差异
senses.definition: the variation in genes among individuals of the same species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种个体之间的基因差异
senses.example: Small populations lose biodiversity at the genetic level even before species disappear.
senses.exampleCN: 小种群在物种消失之前，就已经在遗传层面失去生物多样性。
senses.why: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity defined the term at three levels, and the first extension went inward: variety does not stop between species, it continues among individuals and their genes. A species is itself a pool of differences.
senses.whyCN: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》把该词定义为三个层次，第一次延伸是向内走：多样性并不止于物种之间，它继续存在于个体及其基因之间。一个物种本身就是一池差异。

senses.title: Ecosystem and habitat diversity
senses.titleCN: 生态系统与生境多样性
senses.definition: the variety of ecosystems, habitats, and ecological communities in a region
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区内生态系统、生境与生态群落的多样程度
senses.example: Wetlands, forest and coral reef add ecosystem biodiversity to the same region.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地、森林与珊瑚礁为同一地区增加了生态系统多样性。
senses.why: The third level steps outward: not the organisms but the kinds of place and the communities they form. Difference now applies to habitats, so the same word covers a forest, a marsh and a reef.
senses.whyCN: 第三个层次向外走：不是生物本身，而是地方的类型以及它们形成的群落。差异这时适用于生境，于是同一个词覆盖森林、沼泽与珊瑚礁。

senses.title: The measured level: high or low
senses.titleCN: 多样性水平：可高可低的量
senses.definition: the measured degree of variety in a place, which can be high, low, or declining
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方多样性的可测程度，可高、可低或正在下降
senses.example: The survey recorded low biodiversity in the polluted stretch of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录到河流受污染河段的生物多样性很低。
senses.why: Once a quantity can be counted, it can be compared. Diversity stops being a bare fact and becomes a scale — high, low, rich, poor — which is what field surveys actually report.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可以计数，就可以比较。多样性不再是单纯的事实，而变成一把刻度——高、低、丰富、贫乏——这正是野外调查实际报告的内容。

senses.title: Loss of biodiversity
senses.definition: the decline or disappearance of biological variety, usually through human pressure
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性程度的下降或消失，通常由人类压力造成
senses.example: Habitat clearance is the leading cause of biodiversity loss worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 栖息地清除是世界范围内生物多样性丧失的首要原因。
senses.why: A scale that can fall invites the noun 'loss'. The word now names a public problem, not only a property of a place; conservation supplies the negative frame, and loss becomes the standard collocation.
senses.whyCN: 一个会下跌的刻度自然引出“丧失”这个名词。这个词现在命名的是一种公共问题，而不只是某地的属性；保护话语提供了负面框架，loss 于是成为标准搭配。

senses.title: Conservation hotspot
senses.titleCN: 保护热点：多样性极高又受威胁的地区
senses.definition: a region with exceptionally high biodiversity that is under serious threat
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性异常高、同时面临严重威胁的地区
senses.example: The mountain range is recognised as a global biodiversity hotspot.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉被认定为全球生物多样性热点地区。
senses.why: Where diversity is high and threatened, attention concentrates. Hotspot is the spatial form of that concentration: a place worth naming, mapping and funding, so the word becomes an argument for protection.
senses.whyCN: 在多样性高又受威胁的地方，注意力会集中。hotspot 就是这种集中的空间形态：一个值得命名、绘图和投入资金的地方，于是这个词本身成了一种保护理由。

senses.title: Agricultural biodiversity
senses.titleCN: 农业生物多样性：作物与家畜品种的多样
senses.definition: the variety of crops, livestock breeds, and associated organisms used in farming
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的作物、家畜品种及相关生物的多样性
senses.example: Traditional farms preserve agricultural biodiversity that monocultures lose.
senses.exampleCN: 传统农场保存着单一种植所丧失的农业生物多样性。
senses.why: Humans select plants and animals, so variety also exists among breeds and crop varieties. The compound widens 'life' from wild organisms to cultivated ones, and the word becomes a measure of food-system resilience.
senses.whyCN: 人类对动植物进行选择，所以品种与作物之间也存在多样性。这个复合词把“生命”从野生生物扩展到栽培生物，于是该词成为衡量食物系统韧性的一项指标。

senses.title: Biodiversity as a global commons
senses.titleCN: 作为全球公共资源的生物多样性
senses.definition: biodiversity treated as a shared resource and a subject of international law and policy
senses.definitionCN: 被当作共享资源、并成为国际法与政策对象的生物多样性
senses.example: The treaty treats biodiversity as a common concern of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约把生物多样性视为人类的共同关切。
senses.why: Because genes, species and habitats cross borders, the noun was lifted from ecology into international law. The 1992 Convention made it the name of a shared resource, and the word acquired a political subject as well as an ecological one.
senses.whyCN: 由于基因、物种与生境都跨越国界，这个名词从生态学被提升到国际法。1992 年公约使它成为一种共享资源的名称，这个词于是既有生态学主体，也有政治主体。

senses.title: Diversity in managed or urban land
senses.titleCN: 城市与人工生境中的生物多样性
senses.definition: biological variety measured in cities, restored land, and other human-managed landscapes
senses.definitionCN: 在城市、修复地及其他人类管理景观中测得的生物多样性
senses.example: Green roofs and city parks can raise urban biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色屋顶与城市公园可以提升城市生物多样性。
senses.why: The last extension drops the wilderness assumption: diversity is measured wherever life persists, including cities and restored land. The word becomes a planning target rather than a description of untouched nature.
senses.whyCN: 最后一次延伸丢掉了“荒野”预设：凡有生命存续之处都可测多样性，包括城市与修复地。这个词于是从“未受触及的自然之描述”变成一项规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is not an inherited word. It is a 20th-century scientific compound, clipped from the phrase biological diversity: bio- is Greek, diversity is Latin, and the two were joined in modern English. The earliest written record is disputed.
intro.cn: biodiversity 不是承袭来的词，而是 20 世纪的科学复合词，由短语 biological diversity 截短而成：bio- 是希腊语，diversity 是拉丁语，两者在现代英语里被拼在一起。最早的书面记录存疑。

items.en: bios means 'one's life, course or way of living, lifetime', as opposed to zoē 'animal life'. It comes from PIE *gwei- 'to live'. In English bio- has been used in scientific compounds since about 1800 for 'organic life', though biography keeps the older 'life-story' sense.
items.cn: bios 意为“一个人的生命、生活历程、寿命”，与 zoē“动物生命”相对，来自原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”。英语自约 1800 年起用 bio- 构成科学复合词，表示“有机生命”，但 biography 仍保留更古老的“生平故事”义。

items.en: divertere 'to turn apart' is dis- 'apart' + vertere 'to turn'. Its past participle diversus means 'turned different ways', and diversitas gives 'difference, variety'. English diversity (mid-14c) came through Old French diversete.
items.cn: divertere“转开”是 dis-“分开”+ vertere“转”。其过去分词 diversus 意为“转向各方的”，名词 diversitas 表示“差异、多样”。英语 diversity（14 世纪中）经由古法语 diversete 而来。

items.en: The full phrase was used in ecology and conservation from the 1970s–80s for variety at genetic, species and ecosystem levels. It is a descriptive phrase built from existing words, not a classical term with an ancient pedigree.
items.cn: 完整短语 biological diversity 在 20 世纪 70—80 年代的生态学与保护生物学中用来指基因、物种、生态系统三个层次的多样性。它是由现有词构成的描述性短语，不是有古老传承的经典术语。

items.en: Etymonline dates biodiversity 'by 1988'. The clipped form is often credited to W. G. Rosen in conference material around 1985–86, later printed in 1988; the exact first written use and the first coiner are disputed, and sources differ. Treat the date as approximate.
items.cn: Etymonline 把 biodiversity 记作“by 1988”。这个截短形式常被归到 W. G. Rosen 在 1985—86 年前后的会议材料，后来于 1988 年付印；最早的书面使用与首创者都有争议，各家资料不一。年代只能作大致估计。

items.era: WHY IT IS NOT AN OLD WORD
items.en: There is no Latin biodiversitas and no Greek compound of this shape. The word was built from a living prefix and a living noun to fill a gap in ecology, so its structure stays transparent in a way inherited words are not.
items.cn: 并不存在拉丁语 biodiversitas，也没有这种形状的希腊语复合词。这个词是用活的前缀加活的名词造出来填补生态学的空缺，因此它的结构保持着承袭词所没有的透明性。

items.en: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity fixed the three-level definition and turned the word into a legal and policy term. Later compounds — hotspot, offset, agrobiodiversity — extend it outward from ecology into planning, finance and agriculture.
items.cn: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》确定了三层定义，把这个词变成法律与政策术语。后来的复合词——hotspot、offset、agrobiodiversity——又把它从生态学向外扩展到规划、金融与农业。

note.en: The first group contains the words and phrases most often mistaken for biodiversity itself; the second contains measures of living variety that differ in what they actually count.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被误当成 biodiversity 本身的词与短语；第二组是衡量生命多样性的指标，但各自实际计数的对象不同。

entries.definition: Variety or difference in general. It can describe people, ideas, or tastes; only the bio- prefix makes it about living organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指多样或差异，可指人、想法、口味；只有加上 bio- 才专指生物。

entries.definition: The longer, formal phrase from which biodiversity was clipped. It is the safer term in legal and scientific writing and covers the same three levels.
entries.definitionCN: biodiversity 由之截短而来的较长正式短语。在法律与科学写作中更稳妥，涵盖同样的三个层次。

entries.definition: The total mass of living matter. It shares bio- but measures amount, while biodiversity measures difference.
entries.definitionCN: 活物质的总质量。它共享 bio-，但衡量的是数量，而 biodiversity 衡量的是差异。

entries.definition: A written life of a person, from bio- + graphein 'to write'. It looks like a bio- word but has nothing to do with ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 人物传记，来自 bio- + graphein“书写”。它看起来像 bio- 词，却与生态学无关。

entries.definition: The quality of differing in form or type. Everyday and unmeasured, with no ecological definition behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 形式或类型上存在差异的性质。日常用语，不可量化，背后没有生态学定义。

entries.definition: The number of species in a place. It counts only species, whereas biodiversity also includes genetic and ecosystem variety.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的物种数目。它只数物种，而 biodiversity 还包括遗传与生态系统层面的多样。

entries.definition: The number of individuals of a species. More individuals is not more diversity; a field of one crop can have high abundance and low biodiversity.
entries.definitionCN: 某一物种的个体数量。个体多并不等于多样性高；一块单一种植的田可以个体数量很高而生物多样性很低。

entries.definition: Unevenness in composition or structure across space. It is a measurement of pattern, not the variety of life itself.
entries.definitionCN: 组成或结构在空间上的不均匀。它是格局的度量，而不是生命本身的多样。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek prefix, the real Latin noun, and the real three-level definition.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊前缀、真实的拉丁名词，以及真实的三层定义。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + diversity 'turned apart': life turned into many different forms.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ diversity“转向各方”：生命被分成许多不同的形态。

normal.en: Three levels: genes → species → ecosystems. The word covers all three, and most exam questions test only the first.
normal.cn: 三个层次：基因 → 物种 → 生态系统。这个词覆盖三层，而多数考题只考第一层。

normal.en: Contrast pair: biomass measures amount, biodiversity measures variety. The second half of each word tells you what is measured.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：biomass 量的是数量，biodiversity 量的是多样。两个词的后半部分告诉你衡量的对象。

normal.en: bio- means 'life story' in biography and 'life science' in biology; biodiversity belongs to the science side.
normal.cn: bio- 在 biography 里是“生平故事”，在 biology 里是“生命科学”；biodiversity 属于科学这一侧。

normal.en: The word usually travels with loss, hotspot and conservation, because it names something that can be measured, threatened and protected.
normal.cn: 这个词常与 loss、hotspot、conservation 同行，因为它命名的东西可以被测量、被威胁、被保护。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf with many different books; abundance would be many copies of one book, diversity is many different titles.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架摆着许多不同的书；abundance 是同一本书有很多本，diversity 是有很多不同的书名。

abstract.en: Picture a forest where canopy, understory and soil each hold a different community of life.
abstract.cn: 想象一片森林，树冠层、林下层与土壤各自住着不同的生命群落。

abstract.en: Picture three nested circles: genes inside species, species inside ecosystems. Biodiversity is the whole set of circles, not just the middle one.
abstract.cn: 想象三个同心圆：基因在物种之内，物种在生态系统之内。biodiversity 是整套圆，而不只是中间那一圈。

examples.en: The rainforest supports biodiversity that no plantation can replace.
examples.cn: 雨林所支撑的生物多样性是任何单一林场都无法替代的。

examples.en: Scientists measure biodiversity at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels.
examples.cn: 科学家在遗传、物种和生态系统三个层次上测量生物多样性。

examples.en: The report links biodiversity loss to the draining of local wetlands.
examples.cn: 报告把生物多样性丧失与当地湿地被排干联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命所赐，大（dai）家各有伟（ver）色，提（ti）供多样 → biodiversity 生物多样性

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ 拉丁 diversus“转向各方”构成的 diversity“多样性”；20 世纪仿 biological diversity 截短而成的新造复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one core: difference among living things. The word then widens inward to genes, outward to ecosystems, sideways to measurement and loss, and finally into law and city planning.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个核心：生物之间的差异。这个词随后向内扩展到基因，向外扩展到生态系统，再横向扩展到测量与丧失，最后进入法律与城市规划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life turned into many different forms in one place.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一片土地上的生命分成许多不同的形态。

branches.en: LEVELS OF VARIETY: species differ from one another, and individuals differ genetically inside a species.
branches.cn: 多样的层次：物种之间彼此不同，个体在同一物种内部也有基因差异。

branches.en: PLACES AND CULTIVATION: habitats differ from one another, and farming adds human-selected varieties.
branches.cn: 生境与栽培：生境彼此不同，农业又加入人类选育的品种。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT AND DECLINE: variety becomes a scale with high and low values, and a falling scale becomes loss.
branches.cn: 测量与下降：多样性变成有高低值的刻度，而刻度下跌就成了丧失。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND LAW: threatened richness concentrates attention, and cross-border variety becomes a global commons.
branches.cn: 保护与法律：受威胁的丰富度集中注意力，跨国界的多样性成为全球公共资源。

branches.en: BEYOND WILDNESS: managed and urban land also count, so the word becomes a planning target.
branches.cn: 超越荒野：人工管理与城市土地也计入，于是这个词成为规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is a transparent modern compound: bio- + diversity. Both parts are free-standing or semi-free in English, which is why the word feels self-explaining even to a reader who knows no Latin or Greek.
intro.cn: biodiversity 是一个透明的现代复合词：bio- + diversity。两部分在英语中都能独立或半独立使用，所以即使不懂拉丁语或希腊语，读者也觉得它自我解释。

latinIntro.en: There is no single Latin word behind biodiversity. The prefix is Greek bios; the noun is Latin diversitas, from diversus, past participle of divertere. The compound itself is modern, so its 'etymology' is a join, not an inheritance.
latinIntro.cn: biodiversity 背后没有单个拉丁词。前缀是希腊语 bios；名词是拉丁语 diversitas，出自 divertere 的过去分词 diversus。复合词本身是现代造物，所以它的“词源”是一次拼接，而不是承袭。

items.meaning: the science of life and living things
items.example: She studied biology before turning to ecology.
items.exampleCN: 她在转向生态学之前学的是生物学。

items.meaning: the variety of life at several levels
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性（bio-“生命”+ diversity“多样”）
items.example: The survey mapped biodiversity across the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查绘制了山谷各处的生物多样性。

items.meaning: having a high variety of living things
items.meaningCN: 生物多样的；生物种类丰富的
items.example: The delta is one of the most biodiverse regions in Asia.
items.exampleCN: 这片三角洲是亚洲生物多样性最丰富的地区之一。

items.meaning: the diversity of crops and livestock
items.meaningCN: 农业生物多样性（agro-“农田”+ biodiversity）
items.exampleCN: 种子库保护农业生物多样性。

items.meaning: a place of intense activity or concentration
items.meaningCN: 热点（活动或集中程度极高的地点）
items.example: The region is a biodiversity hotspot.
items.exampleCN: 该地区是一个生物多样性热点。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
a large ecological community shaped by climate
items.exampleCN: 苔原是寒冷的生物群系。

items.meaningCN: 多样性；差异（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The region is known for its cultural diversity.
items.exampleCN: 该地区以文化多样性著称。

items.meaning: to make or become more varied
items.meaningCN: 使多样化；分散（-ify 表示“使……化”）

items.meaning: compensation for damage to habitats, usually by restoring or protecting an equivalent area
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性补偿：通过修复或保护等面积生境来弥补损害
items.example: The company funded a biodiversity offset near the mine.
items.exampleCN: 公司出资在矿区附近实施生物多样性补偿。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 转向各方的；各种各样的

definition_zh: n. 传记作者，传记作家
definition_en: a person who writes the life story of another person
core_image: 档案室里堆满来信与旧照片，一个人正把散落的日期排成一条线
scene: 传记作者在档案馆里待了三年，只为查清一个日期。The biographer spent three years in the archives to pin down a single date.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：biographer 指为他人写传记的人；句意是传记作者为查清一个日期在档案里待了三年。

senses.title: A writer of a life story
senses.definition: someone whose work is to tell the story of another person life in a book
senses.definitionCN: 以成书形式讲述他人一生的人
senses.example: Her biographer interviewed forty people who had known her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的传记作者采访了四十位认识她的人。
senses.why: Graphy means writing and bio means life, so a biographer is literally a life-writer.
senses.whyCN: graphy 意为书写，bio 意为生命，biographer 字面就是「书写生命的人」。

senses.title: A researcher who reconstructs a life
senses.definition: a scholar who works from letters, records and interviews to rebuild a life in detail
senses.definitionCN: 依据书信、档案与访谈细致重建某人一生的学者
senses.example: The biographer checked every claim against the parish register.
senses.exampleCN: 这位传记作者把每个说法都对照教区登记簿核对过。
senses.why: A life story is only as good as its evidence, so the writer is also an investigator.
senses.whyCN: 传记的质量取决于证据，因此写作者同时也是调查者。

intro.en: Biographer is Greek bios, life, plus graphein, to write, plus the agent ending -er.
intro.cn: biographer 是希腊语 bios（生命）加 graphein（书写），再接施事词尾 -er。

items.en: Bios means life, the first element in biology and biography.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，是 biology 与 biography 的第一构件。

items.en: Graphein means to scratch or write, the root of graph and paragraph.
items.cn: graphein 意为刻写，是 graph 与 paragraph 的词根。

items.en: Biographia names the writing of a life.
items.cn: biographia 指书写一生。

items.en: English biography settles as the name of the genre.
items.cn: 英语 biography 固定为这一体裁的名称。

items.en: The agent noun appears for the writer of such a book.
items.cn: 施事名词出现，指写这类书的人。

items.en: The word comes to name a recognised line of work.
items.cn: 这个词开始指一门被承认的职业。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -graph- build; the near-meaning group runs from the writer of a life to the keeper of records.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -graph- 构造；近义组从「写一生的人」排到「保存记录的人」。

normalIntro.en: Bio is life and graphy is writing, so a biographer is the one who writes a life.
normalIntro.cn: bio 是生命，graphy 是书写，biographer 就是书写一生的人。

normal.en: Bio- appears in biology, life science.
normal.cn: bio- 出现在 biology，即生命科学。

normal.en: Graph- appears in paragraph, something written.
normal.cn: graph- 出现在 paragraph，即可写出的段落。

normal.en: Add -er and you have the person doing the writing.
normal.cn: 加 -er 就是做书写这件事的人。

normal.en: A biographer needs letters, dates and witnesses.
normal.cn: 传记作者需要书信、日期与证人。

normal.en: One book, one life, and years of archives.
normal.cn: 一本书，一段人生，和数年档案。

abstract.en: A life rebuilt from paper.
abstract.cn: 用纸重建的一生。

abstract.en: Someone else carrying your dates.
abstract.cn: 替你保管日期的人。

abstract.en: A stranger who knows your childhood better than you.
abstract.cn: 比你更熟悉你童年的陌生人。

examples.en: Her biographer found a letter that changed the accepted story.
examples.cn: 她的传记作者找到一封信，改变了公认的说法。

examples.en: Every biographer faces the same problem: what to leave out.
examples.cn: 每个传记作者都面对同一个问题：该舍弃什么。

examples.en: He worked as a biographer before turning to fiction.
examples.cn: 他在转写小说之前从事传记写作。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ graph（写）+ er（人）——把一个人的一生写下来的人，就是传记作者。

root: 希腊 bios（生命）+ graphein（书写）+ -er（做……的人）

sensesIntro.en: The writer and the researcher are the same person seen twice: one at the desk, one in the archive.
sensesIntro.cn: 「写作者」与「考据者」是同一个人被看两次：一次坐在书桌前，一次待在档案里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters, photographs and dates spread across a desk until a life lines up
core.cn: 核心意象：来信、照片与日期铺满桌面，直到一生被排成一条线

branches.en: Forty interviews for one chapter.
branches.cn: 为一章做的四十次访谈。

branches.en: A manuscript with a life inside it.
branches.cn: 装着一生的手稿。

branches.en: A parish register checked twice.
branches.cn: 被核对两遍的教区登记簿。

branches.en: A footnote that took three years.
branches.cn: 花了三年才写成的一条脚注。

branches.en: Writing that must be proved before it is told.
branches.cn: 必须先被证实才能被讲述的书写。

intro.en: Biographer is two Greek roots and an English agent ending; the list below builds the writing vocabulary around it.
intro.cn: biographer 由两个希腊词根加一个英语施事词尾构成；下面列出围绕它的书写词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek graphein is to write, bios is life, and autos is self.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 graphein 意为书写，bios 意为生命，autos 意为自身。

latinEntries.exampleCN: graphein 产生 graph 与 biography。
bios 产生 biology 与 biography。

definition_zh: 传记；传记文学；生平记述
definition_en: an account of a person's life written by someone else
core_image: 一个人的一生被装订成厚厚一册，由他人执笔
scene: 博物馆纪念展旁边开了一家小书店。She spent five years writing the biography of the poet.
sceneCN: 这里 biography 是「传记」（第 1 个义项：他人所写的生平记述）；句意是她花五年为诗人立传。

derivatives.zh: biography 的形容词，义为「传记的；关于生平的」
biography 的缩略，义为「小传；简介」

senses.title: A written life of a person
senses.definition: a book or article telling the story of someone's life, written by another
senses.definitionCN: 由他人执笔、讲述某人生平的书籍或文章
senses.example: She spent five years writing the biography of the poet.
senses.exampleCN: 她花五年为诗人立传。
senses.why: Greek bios means life and graphein means to write: the writing of a life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 bios 意为「生命」，graphein 意为「书写」，合即「书写一生」。

senses.title: Lives as a literary genre
senses.definition: the literary genre of life-writing as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为文体的传记写作整体
senses.example: Biography blends history with storytelling.
senses.exampleCN: 传记文学融历史与叙事于一体。
senses.why: One written life stands for all life-writing.
senses.whyCN: 一部传记可代指整个传记文体。

senses.title: The events of a life
senses.definition: the course of a person's life as a set of facts
senses.definitionCN: 作为事实总和的某人一生经历
senses.example: The film sticks closely to the scientist's biography.
senses.exampleCN: 影片紧贴这位科学家的真实生平。
senses.why: The life itself can be called by the word for its record.
senses.whyCN: 一生本身可借其记录之名来称呼。

senses.title: A short life-sketch
senses.definition: a brief account of a life, as in a program or application
senses.definitionCN: 简短生平介绍，如节目册或申请材料中的
senses.example: Each speaker's biography appeared in the program.
senses.exampleCN: 每位讲者的小传都印在手册里。
senses.why: The full book shrinks to a paragraph.
senses.whyCN: 整部书缩为一段文字。

senses.title: Ancient lives tradition
senses.definition: the classical tradition of lives, from Plutarch onward
senses.definitionCN: 自普鲁塔克以降的古典传记传统
senses.example: His essay compares ancient biography with modern.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文章比较古今传记传统。
senses.why: The genre names its own history.
senses.whyCN: 文体之名亦涵盖其自身的历史。

senses.title: A life used for interpretation
senses.definition: a person's life used to explain their work or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 以作者生平解读其作品或思想
senses.example: The critic rejected purely biographical reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这位批评家拒绝纯传记式解读。
senses.why: The life story becomes a critical key.
senses.whyCN: 生平成为解读作品的钥匙。

senses.title: Biography on screen
senses.definition: a filmed or dramatized account of a life
senses.definitionCN: 以影像呈现的生平记述
senses.example: The channel aired a biography of the explorer.
senses.exampleCN: 频道播出了这位探险家的传记纪录片。
senses.why: Writing-of-a-life transfers to other media.
senses.whyCN: 「书写一生」转移至其他媒介。

senses.title: Collective biographies
senses.definition: works gathering many lives, as national or group biographies
senses.definitionCN: 汇集多人生平的著作，如国家传记辞典
senses.example: The national biography runs to sixty volumes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部国家传记多达六十卷。
senses.why: Many lives bound together keep the same name.
senses.whyCN: 多部小传合订仍沿用此名。
