senses.title: Relating to living organisms
senses.titleCN: 与生物有关的：属于生命体
senses.definition: concerning living things and the processes that keep them alive
senses.definitionCN: 涉及生命体以及维持其生存的过程
senses.example: The reef supports enormous biological richness.
senses.exampleCN: 这片珊瑚礁养育着极其丰富的生物资源。
senses.why: Biological is built on Greek bios 'life'. Its widest sense simply marks anything that belongs to living matter rather than to machines or minerals.
senses.whyCN: biological 建立在希腊语 bios“生命”上。它最宽的义项只是标记某物属于生命物质，而不是机器或矿物。

senses.title: Relating to the science of biology
senses.titleCN: 生物学的：属于这门学科
senses.definition: concerning the academic study of living things
senses.definitionCN: 涉及对生命体的学术研究
senses.example: The paper was published in a biological journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份生物学杂志上。
senses.why: Once biology became the name of a science, its adjective marked whatever belonged to that discipline: journals, methods, theories.
senses.whyCN: 当 biology 成为一门学科的名称后，它的形容词就标记属于该学科的一切：期刊、方法、理论。

senses.title: Related by blood
senses.titleCN: 血缘的：生物学意义上的亲属
senses.definition: genetically related, as opposed to related by adoption or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 有基因联系的，相对于收养或婚姻关系而言
senses.example: She traced her biological father through a DNA test.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过 DNA 检测找到了亲生父亲。
senses.why: Modern medicine separates social kinship from genetic kinship. Biological marks the kinship carried in the body rather than created by law or care.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学把社会亲属关系与基因亲属关系分开。biological 标记的是身体里携带的亲属关系，而不是法律或抚养建立的。

senses.title: Innate or rooted in body chemistry
senses.definition: arising from the body's natural processes rather than from learning or choice
senses.definitionCN: 来自身体自然过程，而非学习或选择
senses.example: Humans have a biological drive to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 人类有睡眠的生物驱动力。
senses.why: If a behaviour comes from the organism's own machinery, it is biological rather than cultural. The word points down to the body as the cause.
senses.whyCN: 如果一种行为来自生命体自身的机制，它就是 biological 而非文化的。这个词把原因指向身体。

senses.title: Using living organisms
senses.titleCN: 利用生物的：以活体为工具
senses.definition: describing a method that uses living organisms to do work, such as pest control or waste treatment
senses.definitionCN: 描述利用活体完成工作的方式，如害虫防治或废物处理
senses.example: Biological control reduced the aphid population without pesticides.
senses.exampleCN: 生物防治在不使用农药的情况下减少了蚜虫数量。
senses.why: The adjective marks the means, not just the subject: the agent doing the work is itself alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记的是手段而不只是主题：执行工作的主体本身就是活的。

senses.title: Describing biological weapons
senses.titleCN: 生物武器的：用病原体作战
senses.definition: relating to weapons or warfare that use pathogens or toxins to harm people, animals, or plants
senses.definitionCN: 涉及使用病原体或毒素伤害人、动物或植物的武器或战争
senses.example: The treaty bans the development of biological weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约禁止开发生物武器。
senses.why: The life sciences are turned toward destruction. Biological here names the material used as a weapon: living pathogens.
senses.whyCN: 生命科学被转向破坏。这里 biological 命名的是被当作武器的材料：活的病原体。

senses.title: Biological clock or rhythm
senses.titleCN: 生物钟：体内的周期节律
senses.definition: describing the internal timing system that regulates daily or seasonal rhythms
senses.definitionCN: 描述调节昼夜或季节节律的体内计时系统
senses.example: Night shifts disrupted his biological clock.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班打乱了他的生物钟。
senses.why: A clock is a mechanism that keeps time. The body has one built from biological processes, so the metaphor takes the adjective literally.
senses.whyCN: 钟是计时的机制。身体有一套由生物过程构成的钟，因此这个比喻其实把形容词用得很字面。

senses.title: Biological sample or specimen
senses.titleCN: 生物样本：用于研究的活体材料
senses.definition: describing material taken from a living organism for scientific testing
senses.definitionCN: 描述从生命体取出、用于科学检测的材料
senses.example: The lab stores biological samples at very low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在极低温度下保存生物样本。
senses.why: Research needs material that still carries the marks of life. Biological marks the origin of the sample in an organism.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要仍带有生命痕迹的材料。biological 标记样本来源于生命体。

intro.en: Biological is the adjective of biology, a word coined at the beginning of the 19th century from two Greek elements. Its history shows a new science naming itself and then lending its adjective to blood relation, weapons, clocks, and samples.
intro.cn: biological 是 biology 的形容词，而 biology 是 19 世纪初用两个希腊成分新造的词。它的历史显示：一门新科学先给自己命名，再把形容词借给血缘、武器、生物钟和样本。

items.en: Biology was coined independently around 1802 by the French naturalist Lamarck and the German naturalist Treviranus. The adjective biological followed as the science acquired a name.
items.cn: biology 约在 1802 年由法国博物学家拉马克和德国博物学家特雷维拉努斯分别提出。随着这门科学有了名字，形容词 biological 也随后出现。

items.en: Bios meant 'life, course of life'. It is generally traced to a PIE root meaning 'to live', though the deeper reconstruction is not directly attested.
items.cn: bios 意为“生命、生命历程”。它一般被追溯到表示“活着”的原始印欧语词根，但更深层的重构缺乏直接文献证据。

items.en: -logia meant 'the study of', from logos 'word, reason, account'. Biology is literally 'the account of life'.
items.cn: -logia 意为“对……的研究”，来自 logos“言说、理性、论述”。biology 字面就是“关于生命的论述”。

items.en: The compound was formed in scientific Latin as biologia before passing into French, German, and English. The elements are Greek, but the coinage is modern.
items.cn: 这个复合词先在科学拉丁语中形成 biologia，再传入法语、德语和英语。成分是希腊语，但造词本身是现代的。

items.en: Biological first meant 'of the science of life'. It then widened to 'of living things in general', and in the 20th century acquired the sense 'related by blood'.
items.cn: biological 最初意为“生命科学的”。随后扩展到“一般生命体的”，并在 20 世纪获得“有血缘关系的”这一义项。

items.en: Biography, biosphere, biodiversity, and antibiotic all use bios 'life'. Symbiosis uses bios twice: 'living together'. Biology and biological share the same root but differ in part of speech.
items.cn: biography、biosphere、biodiversity、antibiotic 都使用 bios“生命”。symbiosis 用了两次 bios：“共同生活”。biology 与 biological 同根，只是词性不同。

note.en: The first group is the biology word family; the second collects adjectives that also describe what is alive, built-in, or inherited.
note.cn: 第一组是 biology 词族；第二组收同样描述“活的、内置的、遗传的”的形容词。

entries.definition: the science of living things. Biological is its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生命体的科学。biological 是它的形容词。

entries.definition: a scientist who studies living things. The -ist suffix marks the person.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生命体的科学家。-ist 后缀标记从事者。

entries.definition: in biological terms; from the point of view of biology. It is the adverb of biological.
entries.definitionCN: 从生物学角度；在生物学上。它是 biological 的副词。

entries.definition: relating to carbon-based living matter, or grown without chemicals. It overlaps with biological when describing material, but not when describing blood relation.
entries.definitionCN: 与碳基生命物质有关的，或不用化学品培育的。描述物质时与 biological 重叠，但描述血缘时不重叠。

entries.definition: not dead; currently alive. Living is a plain state word, while biological names the scientific frame.
entries.definitionCN: 未死的；活着的。living 是朴素的状态词，biological 则点明科学框架。

entries.definition: present from birth rather than learned. It overlaps with biological in the sense 'built into the body'.
entries.definitionCN: 出生即有的，而非习得的。它与 biological 的“写进身体里”这一义项重叠。

entries.definition: relating to genes or heredity. It is narrower than biological: all genetic relations are biological, but not all biological facts are genetic.
entries.definitionCN: 与基因或遗传有关的。它比 biological 更窄：所有遗传关系都是生物性的，但并非所有生物事实都是遗传的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: bios 'life', -logia 'study', -ical 'relating to', and the pair biology/biologist.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：bios“生命”、-logia“研究”、-ical“与……有关”，以及 biology/biologist 这对词。

normal.en: Bios means 'life' and -logia means 'study': biology is the study of life, and biological means 'relating to it'.
normal.cn: bios 是“生命”，-logia 是“研究”：biology 是研究生命，biological 是“与之相关的”。

normal.en: The adjective adds -ical to biology, just as historic adds -al to history.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是 biology 加 -ical，就像 historic 是 history 加 -al。

normal.en: Biological parent marks the parent connected by genes, while adoptive parent marks the parent connected by care and law.
normal.cn: biological parent 是由基因连接的父母，adoptive parent 是由抚养与法律连接的父母。

normal.en: A biological clock is literally a clock made of biological processes, not a machine.
normal.cn: biological clock 字面上是由生物过程构成的钟，而不是机器。

normal.en: Biological warfare uses living pathogens as weapons; the adjective names the material, not the science.
normal.cn: biological warfare 把活的病原体当武器；形容词命名的是材料，而不是学科。

abstract.en: The word draws a line between what is given by the body and what is made by culture, law, or learning.
abstract.cn: 这个词划出一条线：一边是身体给定的，一边是文化、法律或学习造就的。

abstract.en: Biology is a modern science, but its adjective now reaches far beyond the laboratory — into family, instincts, and weapons.
abstract.cn: biology 是一门现代科学，但它的形容词早已越出实验室——进入家庭、本能和武器。

abstract.en: Whenever biological is used, something is being explained by referring down to the organism rather than up to society.
abstract.cn: 每当使用 biological，都是在把解释指向下面的生命体，而不是上面的社会。

examples.en: The lake's biological health improved after the clean-up.
examples.cn: 清理之后，湖泊的生物健康状况改善了。

examples.en: Some behaviours are biological, but they are still shaped by culture.
examples.cn: 有些行为是生物性的，但仍受文化塑造。

examples.en: The laboratory handles biological material under strict safety rules.
examples.cn: 实验室在严格的安全规则下处理生物材料。

dict_mnemonic.text: “拜欧逻辑扣”——拜欧用逻辑扣住生命（bio）的每个细节 → biological 生物的、生物学的

root: 由 biology 加 -ical 构成；biology 由希腊语 bios“生命”+ -logia“研究”组成，核心是“与生命或生命科学有关”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of biological, all radiating from bios 'life': the science of life, living matter, blood relation, inborn drives, living tools, pathogens as weapons, internal clocks, and laboratory samples.
sensesIntro.cn: biological 的八个义项都从 bios“生命”辐射出来：生命科学、生命物质、血缘、先天驱力、活体工具、病原体武器、体内时钟和实验室样本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree of life growing out of a single cell, with one adjective naming everything connected to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：从单个细胞长出的生命树，一个形容词命名与它相连的一切。

chain: LIFE USED AS TOOL OR WEAPON

branches.en: LIFE AND THE SCIENCE: living organisms in general, and the academic discipline that studies them.
branches.cn: 生命与科学：一般生命体，以及研究它们的学科。

branches.en: KINSHIP: relation carried in genes rather than created by adoption.
branches.cn: 亲属：由基因携带、而非收养建立的关系。

branches.en: BODY MACHINERY: innate drives and the internal clock that times them.
branches.cn: 身体机制：先天驱力，以及为其计时的体内时钟。

branches.en: LIFE AS MATERIAL: organisms used to do work, and samples taken for research.
branches.cn: 作为材料的生命：被用来工作的生物，以及用于研究的样本。

branches.en: LIFE AS WEAPON: pathogens and toxins directed at people, animals, or crops.
branches.cn: 作为武器的生命：指向人、动物或作物的病原体与毒素。

intro.en: Biological is biology + -ical. The productive pattern is bio- 'life' plus a stem, then -logy, -logist, -logical, or -ically.
intro.cn: biological 是 biology + -ical。能产的模式是 bio-“生命”加词干，再加 -logy、-logist、-logical 或 -ically。

latinIntro.en: The elements are Greek, but the compound was coined in New Latin as biologia. Latin and Greek bios is the shared source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分是希腊语，但复合词是在新拉丁语中造出的 biologia。拉丁语与希腊语的 bios 是整个词族的共同来源。

items.meaning: a scientist who studies living things
items.meaningCN: 生物学家（-logist 表示研究者）
items.example: The biologist tagged the birds for tracking.
items.exampleCN: 生物学家给鸟戴上标签以便追踪。

items.meaning: from a biological point of view
items.meaningCN: 生物学上；从生物学角度
items.example: Biologically, the two species are closely related.
items.exampleCN: 从生物学上看，这两个物种关系很近。

items.meaning: biological; also a drug made from living material
items.meaningCN: 生物的；也可作名词指生物制剂
items.example: The patient responded well to the biologic.
items.exampleCN: 患者对这种生物制剂反应良好。

items.meaningCN: 生物制剂（复数，医药用语）
items.example: Biologics are often more expensive than small-molecule drugs.
items.exampleCN: 生物制剂通常比小分子药物更贵。

items.meaning: medicine based on biology and physiology
items.meaningCN: 生物医学（bio- 表示生命）
items.exampleCN: 该研究所专注于生物医学。

items.meaning: the variety of living things in a place
items.example: The forest is a hotspot of biodiversity.
items.exampleCN: 这片森林是生物多样性热点地区。

items.meaning: the zone of the earth where life exists
items.meaningCN: 生物圈（生命存在的地球区域）
微生物学（micro- 表示“微小”）
items.example: Microbiology explains how the infection spreads.
items.exampleCN: 微生物学解释了感染如何传播。

items.meaning: a substance that kills or stops bacteria
items.meaningCN: 抗生素（anti- 表示“对抗”，bio- 表示“生命”）

latinEntries.meaningCN: 生物学（新拉丁语造词，成分来自希腊语）

definition_zh: 生物学家；研究生命现象的科学工作者
definition_en: a scientist who studies living organisms and the processes of life
core_image: 一个人俯身在显微镜与野外记录本之间，把活的东西写进知识
scene: 他每周从湖里取一次水样，一取就是一整年。A biologist took water samples from the lake every week for a year.
sceneCN: 这里 biologist 是「生物学家」（第 1 个义项：研究生命现象的科学工作者）；句意：一位生物学家在一年里每周都从湖里取水样。场景要点：湖泊、采样瓶、显微镜、记录本、防水靴。

pos.zh: 生物学家；生物学研究者

derivatives.zh: 生物学者（1865 年出现的旧式竞争说法，今罕用）

senses.title: A scientist of living things
senses.titleCN: 生物学家：研究生命现象的人
senses.definition: a scientist who studies living organisms and life processes
senses.definitionCN: 研究生物与生命过程的科学家
senses.example: A biologist took water samples from the lake every week.
senses.exampleCN: 一位生物学家每周从湖里取水样。
senses.why: bio- is 'life', -logy is 'study', and -ist is 'one who practises'. The suffix makes a person out of a discipline: the biologist is the human face of biology, and the object of study is anything alive.
senses.whyCN: bio- 是“生命”，-logy 是“学科”，-ist 是“从事者”。这个后缀把一门学科变成一个人：生物学家就是生物学的面孔，而研究对象是一切活的东西。

senses.title: The laboratory researcher
senses.titleCN: 实验室生物学家：在台前做实验的人
senses.definition: a biologist who works mainly in a laboratory, using experiments and instruments
senses.definitionCN: 主要在实验室工作、使用实验与仪器的生物学家
senses.example: The biologist spent the morning at the microscope, counting cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生物学家在显微镜前度过了一上午，数细胞。
senses.why: Modern biology is largely experimental, so the default picture of a biologist became a person at a bench. The word names the profession rather than the place, but bench work supplies its most familiar scene.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物学很大程度上是实验性的，所以生物学家的默认形象变成了实验台前的人。这个词命名的是职业而不是地点，但实验台提供了它最熟悉的场景。

senses.title: The field biologist
senses.titleCN: 野外生物学家：在自然中观察的人
senses.definition: a biologist who studies organisms in their natural habitats rather than in a lab
senses.definitionCN: 在自然栖息地而非实验室研究生物的科学家
senses.example: Field biologists camped in the valley to record bird calls at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 野外生物学家在山谷里扎营，记录黎明时的鸟鸣。
senses.why: The other half of the discipline works outdoors. The same title covers both because the object — living things — is the same; only the method and the setting change.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的另一半在户外工作。同一个头衔覆盖两边，因为对象——活的东西——相同，变化的只是方法与场景。

senses.title: A branch specialist
senses.titleCN: 分支生物学家：海洋、分子、细胞等
senses.definition: a biologist identified by the branch of biology they specialize in
senses.definitionCN: 以所专攻的生物学分支来称呼的生物学家
senses.example: A marine biologist explained why the reef was bleaching.
senses.exampleCN: 一位海洋生物学家解释了珊瑚礁为何白化。
senses.why: Biology split into branches, and English simply puts the branch before biologist: marine biologist, molecular biologist. The head noun still marks the person, while the first word narrows the field.
senses.whyCN: 生物学分成许多分支，英语直接把分支放在 biologist 前面：marine biologist、molecular biologist。中心名词仍标记“人”，前面的词则缩小领域。

senses.title: The -ist pattern: practitioner of a discipline
senses.definition: the general pattern by which -ist turns the name of a discipline into the name of the person who practises it
senses.definitionCN: -ist 把学科名称变成从业者名称的一般构词模式
senses.example: Botanists, zoologists and biologists all belong to the same -ist family.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家、动物学家和生物学家都属于同一个 -ist 词族。
senses.why: -ist comes from Greek -istēs, an agent ending. Attaching it to -logy produces 'one who does the study'. The word therefore says what the person practises, not what they are like.
senses.whyCN: -ist 来自希腊语 -istēs，是施事词尾。把它加到 -logy 上就产生“从事这项研究的人”。所以这个词说的是“做什么”，而不是“是什么样的人”。

senses.title: The older sense: a student of life
senses.titleCN: 早期义：研究生命之学的人（1813）
senses.definition: the original English sense: a student of the science of life, with human life especially in view
senses.definitionCN: 英语最早的含义：研究生命之学的人，尤其着眼于人的生命
senses.example: The word biologist was first used in 1813 for a student of the science of life.
senses.exampleCN: biologist 一词在 1813 年最早用来指研究生命之学的人。
senses.why: The earliest English use (1813) still carried the Greek sense of bios as a person's life; the modern professional sense is recorded only by 1859. The word began as 'learner' and later became 'profession'.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的使用（1813）仍带着希腊语 bios“一个人的生命”这层意思；现代职业义直到 1859 年才有记录。这个词从“学习者”开始，后来才成为“职业”。

senses.title: Conservation and applied biologist
senses.titleCN: 保护与应用生物学家：为管理生命而研究
senses.definition: a biologist whose work is directed at protecting or managing species and habitats
senses.definitionCN: 工作指向保护或管理物种与栖息地的生物学家
senses.example: Conservation biologists argue that protecting habitat protects species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护生物学家主张，保护栖息地就是保护物种。
senses.why: When biology is applied to managing species, the title gains a purpose: the biologist is not only describing life but defending it. The compound marks that applied role rather than a new kind of science.
senses.whyCN: 当生物学被用于管理物种时，这个头衔多了一层目的：生物学家不仅在描述生命，也在为生命辩护。这个复合词标记的是应用角色，而不是一门新科学。

senses.title: Biologists as a community
senses.titleCN: 生物学界：作为群体的生物学家
senses.definition: the profession or community of biologists, treated as a body of shared opinion
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个共享观点的群体的生物学家职业共同体
senses.example: Biologists generally agree that the warming ocean is shifting fish stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家普遍认为，海洋变暖正在改变鱼类种群分布。
senses.why: The plural without an article names a profession as a body of opinion. This is the collective sense: not one researcher but the discipline speaking, which is why news reports say 'biologists say'.
senses.whyCN: 不带冠词的复数把一种职业命名为一个观点共同体。这是集体义：说话的不是某位研究者，而是整个学科，所以新闻报道会说 biologists say。

senses.title: Attributive: a biologist's view
senses.definition: used before another noun or after 'as' to name the professional lens through which something is seen
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前或 as 之后，指看待某事物时所采用的生物学家视角
senses.example: As a biologist, she sees the garden as a web of interactions.
senses.exampleCN: 作为生物学家，她把花园看成一个相互作用的网络。
senses.why: Before another noun or after 'as', the word labels the lens through which something is seen. It is still a person, but the person now functions as a viewpoint rather than as the subject of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 置于名词前或 as 之后时，这个词标记的是观察事物所用的镜头。它仍然指人，但此时的人作为“视角”起作用，而不是句子的主体。

intro.en: Biologist is biology + -ist. Biology itself is a modern Greek-Latin hybrid coined around 1800, so the whole family is scientific rather than inherited. The exact first coiner of biology is disputed; the date of biologist is better recorded.
intro.cn: biologist 是 biology + -ist。biology 本身是约 1800 年前后造出的希腊—拉丁混合词，所以整个词族是科学造词而非承袭词。biology 的确切首创者存疑，biologist 的年代记录则较清楚。

items.en: bios means 'life, lifetime, way of life' (PIE *gwei- 'to live'), as opposed to zoē 'animal life'. In modern scientific compounds bio- means 'life, living organisms'.
items.cn: bios 意为“生命、寿命、生活方式”（原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”），与 zoē“动物生命”相对。在现代科学复合词里，bio- 表示“生命、生物”。

items.en: logos means 'word, account, reason'. The derived -logia means 'the study of', and English -logy comes through Latin -logia. Biology is therefore 'the account or study of life'.
items.cn: logos 意为“词、叙述、理性”。派生的 -logia 表示“对……的研究”，英语 -logy 经由拉丁语 -logia 而来。因此 biology 就是“关于生命的论述或研究”。

items.en: The compound biology was suggested in 1802 by the German naturalist Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus and introduced in French that same year by Lamarck; the two seem to have hit on it independently. Who first coined it cannot be settled. English biology is recorded in 1819.
items.cn: 复合词 biology 由德国博物学家 Gottfried Reinhold Treviranus 于 1802 年提出，同年由拉马克在法语中引入；两人似乎是独立想到的。谁最先造出这个词无法确定。英语 biology 记录于 1819 年。

items.en: biologist is recorded from 1813, meaning 'a student of the science of life'. The earliest use refers to human life, in the Greek sense of bios; the modern sense 'one skilled in or a student of biology' is recorded by 1859.
items.cn: biologist 自 1813 年有记录，意为“研究生命之学的人”。最早用法指人的生命，取希腊语 bios 之义；现代义“精通或研究生物学的人”到 1859 年才有记录。

items.en: -ist 'one who does or makes' comes from French -iste and Latin -ista, from Greek -istēs, an agent ending built on verb stems. It makes biologist the person who practises what biology names.
items.cn: -ist“从事者”来自法语 -iste、拉丁语 -ista，再往上为希腊语 -istēs——建立在动词词干上的施事前缀。它使 biologist 成为“实践 biology 所示之事的人”。

items.en: Biography is bio- + graphein 'to write', literally 'life-writing', and its person is a biographer. Biology is bio- + -logy 'study', and its person is a biologist. The shared bio- is real, but the second element decides the word: writing versus studying.
items.cn: biography 是 bio- + graphein“书写”，字面“写生命”，其指人名词是 biographer。biology 是 bio- + -logy“研究”，其指人名词是 biologist。共享的 bio- 是真实的，但第二成分决定词义：书写还是研究。

note.en: The first group contains forms built on the same bio- prefix that are easily mistaken for the person; the second contains nearby professions that differ in scope or object.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 bio- 前缀构成、容易被误当成“指人”的形式；第二组是范围或对象不同的邻近职业。

entries.definition: The science of life. It ends in -logy 'study', so it names the field; biologist adds -ist to name the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 生命科学。它以 -logy“研究”结尾，命名的是领域；biologist 加 -ist 才命名从业者。

entries.definition: An account of a person's life, from bio- + graphein 'to write'. Its person is a biographer, never a biologist.
entries.definitionCN: 对一个人生平的记述，来自 bio- + graphein“书写”。其指人名词是 biographer，绝不是 biologist。

entries.definition: A rare 19th-century rival for biologist, recorded 1865 and now obsolete. It shows that -ist won the competition.
entries.definitionCN: 19 世纪与 biologist 竞争的罕见说法，1865 年有记录，今已废弃。它说明 -ist 赢下了这场竞争。

entries.definition: Relating to life or living things, from Greek biōtikos. It is an adjective, so it can never name the scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 与生命或生物有关的，来自希腊语 biōtikos。它是形容词，绝不能指科学家。

entries.definition: A researcher in any life science, including biomedicine and biochemistry. Broader than biologist, which usually points to organism-level study.
entries.definitionCN: 任何生命科学领域的研究者，包括生物医学与生物化学。比 biologist 宽，后者通常指生物体层面的研究。

entries.definition: A student of plants and animals through observation, often outside a university. It stresses watching nature rather than running experiments.
entries.definitionCN: 通过观察研究动植物的学者，常在大学之外。它强调观察自然，而不是做实验。

entries.definition: A specialist in animals. It is one branch of biology, so every zoologist is a biologist but not every biologist is a zoologist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究动物的专家。它是生物学的一个分支，所以动物学家都是生物学家，但生物学家不都是动物学家。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies the relations between organisms and their environment. The focus is the system, not the individual organism.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与环境之间关系的科学家。焦点在系统，而不在单个生物体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real branch names, and the real biography contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的分支名称，以及 biography 的真实对比。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + -logy 'study' + -ist 'practitioner': the person who does the study of life.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ -logy“研究”+ -ist“从业者”：从事生命研究的人。

normal.en: Test the ending: -logy is the field, -logist is the person. biology → biologist, geology → geologist.
normal.cn: 看词尾：-logy 是领域，-logist 是人。biology → biologist，geology → geologist。

normal.en: Branch names go before the person: marine, molecular, cell, evolutionary, conservation + biologist.
normal.cn: 分支名放在“人”前面：marine、molecular、cell、evolutionary、conservation + biologist。

normal.en: biography ends in -graphy 'writing', so its person is biographer. Never mix the two second elements.
normal.cn: biography 以 -graphy“书写”结尾，其指人名词是 biographer。不要把两个第二成分混在一起。

normal.en: The word began in 1813 as 'student of life' and only later meant a paid professional; that history explains why it sounds academic.
normal.cn: 这个词 1813 年起初是“研究生命的学生”，后来才指拿薪水的专业人士；这段历史解释了它为何带学术气。

abstract.en: Picture a person standing between a microscope and a muddy boot: lab and field are the two halves of one biologist.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在显微镜和沾泥的靴子之间：实验室与野外是同一个生物学家的两半。

abstract.en: Picture a tree of disciplines: biology is the trunk, and marine, cell, evolutionary biologists are branches bearing the same -ist label.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵学科树：biology 是树干，marine、cell、evolutionary 各支都挂着同一个 -ist 标签。

abstract.en: Picture the suffix as a badge: -ist is pinned on whoever practises the field, so the badge, not the field, makes the person.
abstract.cn: 把后缀想成一枚徽章：谁从事这门领域，-ist 就别在谁身上；造出“人”的是徽章，而不是领域。

examples.en: Biologists still disagree about how many species live in the deep ocean.
examples.cn: 生物学家对深海中有多少物种仍存在分歧。

examples.en: The marine biologist spent three months surveying the coral reef.
examples.cn: 这位海洋生物学家花了三个月调查珊瑚礁。

examples.en: As a biologist, she reads the forest as a set of relationships rather than a collection of trees.
examples.cn: 作为生物学家，她把森林读成一组关系，而不是一堆树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命，欧（o）罗（lo）辑（gi）知识，斯特（st）专门研究 → biologist 生物学家

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ -logia“研究”构成的 biology（约 1802 年新造）+ -ist“从业者”；字面即“研究生命之学的人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one person: someone who studies life. What changes is where they work, which branch they name, whether the word means learner or professional, and whether it speaks for one researcher or the whole discipline.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个人：研究生命的人。变化的是工作地点、所属分支、词义是“学习者”还是“职业”，以及说话的是某位研究者还是整个学科。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who turns living things into knowledge.
core.cn: 核心意象：把活的东西变成知识的人。

branches.en: THE MAKING OF THE WORD: life + study + agent suffix, which is the general -ist pattern.
branches.cn: 词的构成：生命 + 研究 + 施事后缀，也就是 -ist 的一般模式。

branches.en: TWO WORKPLACES: the bench and the field are the two halves of the same profession.
branches.cn: 两个工作场所：实验台与野外是同一职业的两半。

branches.en: SPECIALITY AND PURPOSE: branch names narrow the field, and applied names add a goal.
branches.cn: 分支与目的：分支名缩小领域，应用名增加目标。

branches.en: HISTORICAL LAYER: the earliest sense was 'student of life', not paid professional.
branches.cn: 历史层：最早的义项是“研究生命的学生”，而不是拿薪水的专业人士。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND LENS: the plural can speak for a discipline, and 'as a biologist' names a viewpoint.
branches.cn: 集体与视角：复数可以代表整个学科，as a biologist 则命名一种视角。

intro.en: Biologist is built from three live pieces: bio- (life), -logy (study), -ist (practitioner). Unlike an inherited Latin word, every joint is still visible to a modern reader.
intro.cn: biologist 由三个仍然能产的部分构成：bio-“生命”、-logy“研究”、-ist“从业者”。与承袭的拉丁词不同，每一处接缝对现代读者都仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: The elements come from Greek, not Latin: bios 'life', logos 'account, reason', and -istēs 'one who does'. They entered English through Latin and French forms (-logia, -ista), which is why the endings look Latin even though the roots are Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这些成分来自希腊语而非拉丁语：bios“生命”、logos“叙述、理性”、-istēs“从事者”。它们经由拉丁语和法语形式（-logia、-ista）进入英语，所以词根虽是希腊语，词尾看起来却像拉丁语。

items.example: Biology was her favourite subject at school.
items.exampleCN: 生物学是她上学时最喜欢的科目。

items.example: The biologist recorded the behaviour of the birds.
items.exampleCN: 这位生物学家记录了这些鸟的行为。

items.meaning: relating to biology or living things
items.example: The sample was sent for biological testing.
items.exampleCN: 样本被送去进行生物检测。

items.meaningCN: 从生物学角度；在生物层面
items.example: The two species are biologically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种在生物学上是不同的。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
items.example: Life is concentrated in the biosphere.

items.meaning: a written account of a person's life
items.meaningCN: 传记（bio-“生命”+ -graphy“书写”，第二成分不同）
items.example: She wrote a biography of the chemist.
items.exampleCN: 她写了一部关于这位化学家的传记。

items.meaningCN: 传记作者（与 biologist 的指人后缀不同）
items.exampleCN: 传记作者采访了这家人。

items.meaning: a scientist who studies rocks and the earth
items.example: A geologist dated the rock layer.
items.exampleCN: 一位地质学家测定了岩层的年代。

items.meaningCN: 动物学家（生物学的一个分支）
items.example: The zoologist studied the migration route.
items.exampleCN: 这位动物学家研究了迁徙路线。

items.example: The botanist identified the plant from its leaves.
items.exampleCN: 植物学家根据叶子辨认出这种植物。

latinEntries.meaning: the study of, an account of
agent ending: one who does or practises
latinEntries.meaningCN: 施事后缀：从事、实践某事的人

definition_zh: n. 生物识别技术（指纹、人脸等身份核验）；生物统计学
definition_en: methods of identifying people by measurable body features; also the statistical study of living things
core_image: 一只手指按在玻璃板上，屏幕立刻勾出指纹的纹路
scene: 机场现在用生物识别技术核对旅客与护照。The airport now uses biometrics to match travellers with their passports.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：biometrics 指以身体特征核验身份的技术；句意是机场用生物识别核对旅客与护照。

pos.zh: 生物识别技术；生物统计学

collocations.zh: 对生物识别的隐私担忧

forms.label: 不可数名词（作技术、学科名）

senses.title: Identity checked by body features
senses.definition: technology that identifies a person from a fingerprint, iris, face or voice
senses.definitionCN: 用指纹、虹膜、面部或声音辨认身份的技术
senses.example: The phone unlocks with biometrics rather than a password.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机用生物识别解锁，而不是密码。
senses.why: Metron means measure, so biometrics is the measuring of life for identification.
senses.whyCN: metron 意为测量，biometrics 就是为识别而对生命特征进行的测量。

senses.title: Statistics applied to living things
senses.definition: the branch of statistics that deals with measurements taken from living organisms
senses.definitionCN: 处理生物测量数据的统计学分支
senses.example: Biometrics helped the team separate natural variation from real change.
senses.exampleCN: 生物统计帮助团队把自然波动与真实变化区分开。
senses.why: The plural -ics names a field of study, as in physics and economics.
senses.whyCN: 复数词尾 -ics 表示一门学科，如 physics 与 economics。

intro.en: Biometrics joins Greek bios, life, to metron, measure, with the field-forming ending -ics.
intro.cn: biometrics 把希腊语 bios（生命）与 metron（尺度）连接，再加表示学科的 -ics。

items.en: Bios means life, the first element in biology and biometrics.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，是 biology 与 biometrics 的第一构件。

items.en: Metron means measure, the root of metre and symmetry.
items.cn: metron 意为尺度，是 metre 与 symmetry 的词根。

items.en: Biometry first names the statistical study of living things.
items.cn: biometry 最初指对生物的统计研究。

items.en: Fingerprint and voice matching give the word a security sense.
items.cn: 指纹与声纹比对赋予该词安全领域的含义。

items.en: Consumer devices begin to carry biometric sensors.
items.cn: 消费设备开始搭载生物识别传感器。

items.en: Biometrics now usually means identity checks, not statistics.
items.cn: 现代 biometrics 多指身份核验，而非统计学。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bio- or -metr- build; the near-meaning group gathers the security words that surround identity checks.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bio- 或 -metr- 构造；近义组汇集围绕身份核验的安全词汇。

entries.definition: Relating to body measurement.
The statistical study of living things.
Systems or sets of measurements.
Relating to biology and medicine together.
Recording fingerprints to identify people.
The act of proving who someone is.
The process of verifying a claimed identity.
entries.definitionCN: 核实所声称身份的过程。

entries.definition: Close watching of people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或场所的密切监视。

normalIntro.en: Bios is life and metron is measure, so biometrics measures a living body to say who it is.
normalIntro.cn: bios 是生命，metron 是尺度，biometrics 就是测量活体以判定身份。

normal.en: Metric means measure, as in metric system.
normal.cn: metric 意为测量，如公制 metric system。

normal.en: Bio- means life, so biometric is life measurement.
normal.cn: bio- 意为生命，biometric 就是生命测量。

normal.en: The -ics ending marks a field, like physics.
normal.cn: -ics 词尾表示学科，如 physics。

normal.en: Your fingerprint is a measurement you cannot change.
normal.cn: 指纹是一种你改不掉的测量值。

normal.en: Face, iris, voice, gait: four ways to be measured.
normal.cn: 脸、虹膜、声音、步态：四种被测量的方式。

abstract.en: A body used as a password.
abstract.cn: 被当作密码使用的身体。

abstract.en: Measurement that answers only who.
abstract.cn: 只回答「是谁」的测量。

abstract.en: A key you cannot leave at home.
abstract.cn: 无法忘在家里的钥匙。

examples.en: Banks are adding biometrics to phone banking.
examples.cn: 银行正在给手机银行加入生物识别。

examples.en: Critics warn that biometrics cannot be reset like a password.
examples.cn: 批评者提醒说，生物识别不像密码那样可以重置。

examples.en: Her background is in biometrics rather than security.
examples.cn: 她的背景是生物统计，而不是安全技术。

root: 希腊 bios（生命）+ metron（尺度）+ -ics（学科、技术）

sensesIntro.en: One word carries two eras: the statistician measuring populations and the gate that measures your face.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词背着两个时代：测量群体的统计学家，以及测量你面部的大门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip on glass while a screen traces the whorls of a print
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖按在玻璃上，屏幕勾出指纹的纹路

branches.en: A thumb pressed on a sensor.
branches.cn: 按在传感器上的拇指。

branches.en: A camera measuring the distance between eyes.
branches.cn: 测量两眼间距的摄像头。

branches.en: A table of growth data from a field study.
branches.cn: 野外研究的长势数据表。

branches.cn: 由数千样本画出的曲线。

branches.en: Numbers taken from living bodies.

intro.en: Biometrics is a Greek life-word on a Greek measure-word; the endings below form the vocabulary of measurement.
intro.cn: biometrics 是一个希腊「生命」词加希腊「尺度」词；下面的词缀构成测量词汇。

latinIntro.en: Greek metron is a measure, metria is measurement, and bios is life.

bios 产生 biology 与 biometrics。

definition_zh: n. 生物个体（生态学用语，指一个独立的生物体）
definition_en: an individual living organism, especially as a unit in an ecological or symbiotic relationship
core_image: 显微镜视野里一个单独的细胞体，周围是它的共生伙伴
scene: 样本中的每一个生物个体都与它的共生体一同被记录。Each biont in the sample was recorded together with its symbionts.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：biont 指一个独立的生物个体；句意是样本中每个生物个体都与共生体一起被记录。

senses.title: An individual living organism
senses.definition: a single organism treated as one living unit
senses.definitionCN: 被视为一个生命单位的单个生物体
senses.example: The colony is made of thousands of identical bionts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体由数千个相同的生物个体组成。
senses.why: It was built from Greek bios with the participle ending -on, meaning a living thing.
senses.whyCN: 它由希腊语 bios 加分词词尾 -on 构成，意为「活着的东西」。

senses.title: A unit inside a living partnership
senses.definition: one member of a close association between different organisms
senses.definitionCN: 不同生物紧密共生关系中的一方
senses.example: In the partnership the smaller biont supplies sugar to its host.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种共生关系中，较小的生物个体为宿主提供糖分。
senses.why: Symbiosis is made of partners, and each partner is called a biont.
senses.whyCN: 共生由伙伴组成，每一方都称作一个 biont。

intro.en: Biont is Greek bios, life, plus the participle ending -on, so it means simply a living thing.
intro.cn: biont 是希腊语 bios（生命）加分词词尾 -on，意为「活着的存在者」。

items.en: Bios means life, the root of biology and biont.
items.cn: bios 意为生命，是 biology 与 biont 的词根。

items.en: The ending -on marks a participle, a thing that is.
items.cn: 词尾 -on 是分词标记，表示「存在之物」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology coins short forms for living units.
items.cn: 十九世纪生物学为生命单位造出简短形式。

items.en: The compound symbiont names one partner in a partnership.
items.cn: 复合词 symbiont 指共生关系中的一方。

items.en: Biont is used for an individual in population studies.
items.cn: 二十世纪生态学用 biont 指种群研究中的个体。

items.en: The word survives mainly in compounds and technical prose.
items.cn: 现代该词主要存在于复合词与技术文献中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -biont or bion- shape; the near-meaning group moves from the single organism to the species it belongs to.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -biont 或 bion- 的形状；近义组由单个生物体排到它所属的物种。

entries.definition: An organism living closely with another.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一生物紧密共居的生物。

entries.definition: The design of systems copied from living things.
Relating to artificial body parts.
entries.definitionCN: 与人工身体部件有关的。

entries.definition: All organisms living in one habitat.
A single living thing.
A living animal or being.
A single member of a group.
A group of similar living things.

normalIntro.en: Biont is life plus an ending for a thing that exists, so it names one living unit.
normalIntro.cn: biont 是「生命」加「存在之物」的词尾，因此指一个生命单位。

normal.en: Bio- means life wherever it appears.
normal.cn: bio- 出现在哪里都表示生命。

normal.en: The -ont ending also shows in symbiont.
normal.cn: -ont 词尾也出现在 symbiont 中。

normal.en: A biont is one organism, counted once.
normal.cn: biont 就是一个生物体，计作一个。

normal.en: In a partnership each partner is a biont.
normal.cn: 在共生关系中，每一方都是一个 biont。

normal.en: When ecology says individual, it often means biont.
normal.cn: 生态学说的「个体」，常常就是 biont。

abstract.en: One life, counted as one.
abstract.cn: 一条生命，计作一个。

abstract.en: The smallest living unit in a census.
abstract.cn: 普查中最小的生命单位。

abstract.en: Half of a partnership seen alone.
abstract.cn: 把共生的一半单独来看。

examples.en: Each biont was weighed before the experiment began.
examples.cn: 实验开始前，每个生物个体都称过重量。

examples.en: The fungus and the alga survive as separate bionts in culture.
examples.cn: 真菌与藻类在培养中作为各自独立的生物个体存活。

examples.en: Population counts treat every biont as one data point.
examples.cn: 种群计数把每个生物个体当作一个数据点。

sensesIntro.cn: biont 首先只是一个活物，其次是把同一个活物看作共生关系的一半。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single cell body under the lens, with a partner pressed against it
core.cn: 核心意象：镜下一个单独的细胞体，另有一个伙伴贴在它旁边

branches.en: One cell counted in a sample.
branches.cn: 样本中被数到的单个细胞。

branches.en: One plant standing in a quadrat.
branches.cn: 样方里立着的一株植物。

branches.en: A fungus feeding an alga.
branches.cn: 为藻类供给养分的真菌。

branches.en: Two partners that cannot live apart.
branches.cn: 无法分开生活的两个伙伴。

branches.en: One life seen alone or in a pair.
branches.cn: 单独看或成对看的一条生命。

intro.cn: biont 几乎全是希腊语；下面列出它的词尾与同一词干构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios is life, symbiosis is living together, and -on marks a living thing.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 bios 意为生命，symbiosis 意为共同生活，-on 表示「存在之物」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: bios 产生 biology 与 biont。

definition_zh: 生物圈；生命层；全球生命支持系统
definition_en: the zone of Earth, including land, water and air, in which living things exist
core_image: 一颗裹着薄薄绿色生命膜的蓝色星球，那层膜比苹果皮还薄
scene: 地球表面那层薄薄的活体，决定了我们呼吸的空气。The biosphere is a thin skin on the planet, yet it controls the air we breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 biosphere 指「生物圈」（第 1 个义项：地球上生命存在的整体区域）；句意：生物圈只是这颗行星上薄薄的一层，却控制着我们呼吸的空气。图中可辨识物件：地球剖面、绿色生命层、大气薄层标注。

pos.zh: 生物圈；生命层；全球生命支持系统（通常作单数，带定冠词 the biosphere；也可指其他行星的生命圈）

derivatives.zh: 生物区系；一个地区的全部生物

senses.title: The Living Zone of Earth
senses.titleCN: 生物圈：地球上生命存在的整体区域
senses.definition: the zone of Earth where living things exist, including land, water and air
senses.definitionCN: 地球上生命存在的区域，包括陆地、水与空气
senses.example: The biosphere is a thin skin on the planet, yet it controls the air we breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈只是这颗行星上薄薄的一层，却控制着我们呼吸的空气。
senses.why: Greek bios 'life' plus sphaira 'ball' gives 'the life-ball'. The word treats all living things together as one layer of the planet, not as a list of species.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 bios「生命」加 sphaira「球」构成「生命之球」。这个词把所有生物合起来当作行星的一层，而不是一张物种清单。

senses.title: Life on Another World
senses.definition: the living layer of any planet, real or imagined
senses.definitionCN: 任何行星上真实或想象的生命层
senses.example: A Mars biosphere, if it ever existed, may survive only underground.
senses.exampleCN: 火星生物圈若曾存在，可能只幸存于地下。
senses.why: Once the word means a layer rather than a place, it can be detached from Earth. Planetary science uses it for the total living system of any world.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指「一层」而不是「一个地方」，它就能与地球脱离；行星科学用它指任何世界的整体生命系统。

senses.title: The Ecological Layer
senses.definition: the living layer studied as part of the Earth system
senses.definitionCN: 作为地球系统一部分来研究的生命层
senses.example: Ecologists model the biosphere as one component of the Earth system.
senses.exampleCN: 生态学家把生物圈建模为地球系统的一个组分。
senses.why: Earth-system science splits the planet into spheres: atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere. The word then names one box in a diagram of interacting boxes.
senses.whyCN: 地球系统科学把行星分成若干圈：大气圈、水圈、岩石圈与生物圈；此时这个词命名的是相互作用框图里的一个方框。

senses.title: A Sealed Living System
senses.titleCN: 封闭生物圈：人工封闭生态系统
senses.definition: a closed experimental system that contains living things and recycles its materials
senses.definitionCN: 包含生物并循环其物质的人工封闭系统
senses.example: The sealed biosphere lasted only two years.
senses.exampleCN: 那个封闭生物圈只维持了两年。
senses.why: Experiments such as Biosphere 2 borrowed the name for a sealed miniature world. The test is whether life can keep its own conditions without outside help.
senses.whyCN: 生物圈二号一类实验借用了这个名字，指封闭的微型世界；它检验的是生命能否在没有外界帮助的情况下维持自身条件。

senses.title: Life as a Planetary Component
senses.titleCN: 作为行星组分的生命总体
senses.definition: the total living component of a planet, considered as one system
senses.definitionCN: 一颗行星的全部生命组分，被视为一个系统
senses.example: The biosphere and the atmosphere exchange carbon every second.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈与大气每时每刻都在交换碳。
senses.why: Here the emphasis is on exchange: life is not only inside the environment but helps make it. This sense underlies the idea that life regulates the planet's chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调交换：生命不只在环境之中，还参与制造环境。这一义项支撑了「生命调节行星化学」的观点。

senses.title: Total Living Support
senses.definition: the whole system that keeps conditions suitable for life
senses.definitionCN: 维持适宜生命条件的整个系统
senses.example: Protecting the biosphere is not the same as protecting a few species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护生物圈并不等于保护少数几个物种。
senses.why: Policy language uses the word for the life-support system as a whole. The shift is from a place to a function: the biosphere is what keeps conditions livable.
senses.whyCN: 政策语言用这个词指整个生命支持系统；重心从「地点」转向「功能」：生物圈是维持条件宜居的那套东西。

senses.title: A Reserve for Life
senses.titleCN: 生物圈保护区：受保护的样板区
senses.definition: an area designated to protect ecosystems and to study them
senses.definitionCN: 为保护并研究生态系统而划定的区域
senses.example: The valley was named a biosphere reserve in 1998.
senses.exampleCN: 该山谷于 1998 年被列为生物圈保护区。
senses.why: International programmes turned the abstract noun into a label on a map. A biosphere reserve is not the whole biosphere but a local sample of it, managed for both use and study.
senses.whyCN: 国际计划把这个抽象名词变成地图上的标记；生物圈保护区不是整个生物圈，而是它的一个地方样本，兼顾利用与研究。

senses.title: The Object of a Science
senses.titleCN: 作为研究对象的全球生态系
senses.definition: the global ecosystem taken as the object of a scientific field
senses.definitionCN: 作为某一科学领域研究对象的全球生态系统
senses.example: Biosphere science connects biology with climate and chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 生物圈科学把生物学与气候、化学联系起来。
senses.why: A name for a layer can become the name of a field. The word then appears in course titles and journal names, where it marks a scale rather than a single object.
senses.whyCN: 一个圈层的名称可以变成一个领域的名称；此时该词出现在课程名与期刊名里，标出的是一个尺度，而不是单一对象。

intro.en: Biosphere joins Greek bios 'life' and sphaira 'ball, sphere'. It was coined by the geologist Eduard Suess in 1875 and later popularized by Vladimir Vernadsky.
intro.cn: biosphere 由希腊 bios「生命」与 sphaira「球、球体」组成。该词由地质学家 Eduard Suess 于 1875 年造出，后由 Vladimir Vernadsky 推广。

items.en: Bios meant 'life, mode of life'. It appears in biology, biography, biota and antibiotic, though the compound meanings differ in each.
items.cn: bios 意为「生命、生活方式」，出现在 biology、biography、biota、antibiotic 中，但各复合词的含义并不相同。

items.en: Sphaira meant 'ball, globe'. Latin took it as sphaera, and English gets sphere, spherical and the -sphere of atmosphere and hydrosphere.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球、球体」。拉丁语借作 sphaera，英语由此得到 sphere、spherical，以及 atmosphere、hydrosphere 中的 -sphere。

items.en: Eduard Suess coined Biosphere in 1875 to name the layer of Earth in which life occurs. His word treated life as a stratum comparable to rock or water, a geological rather than a poetic idea.
items.cn: Eduard Suess 于 1875 年造出 Biosphere，用来指地球上生命出现的那一层。他的词把生命视为可与岩石或水相提并论的层，这是一个地质学观念，而非诗意比喻。

items.en: Vladimir Vernadsky developed the concept in the early twentieth century, arguing that life actively shapes the planet's chemistry. His work made the word common in ecology.
items.cn: Vladimir Vernadsky 在二十世纪初发展了这一概念，主张生命主动塑造行星的化学；他的工作使该词在生态学中通行。

items.en: UNESCO's biosphere reserve programme and Earth-system science gave the word a policy and a modelling life. It now names a layer, a global system and a protected area at once.
items.cn: 联合国教科文组织的生物圈保护区计划与地球系统科学赋予该词政策与建模上的生命；如今它同时指一个圈层、一个全球系统与一片保护区。

note.en: The first group separates the neighboring sphere terms and the smaller ecological units. The second holds near-synonyms that name life at global scale.
note.cn: 第一组区分相邻的圈层术语与更小的生态单位；第二组是命名全球尺度生命的近义词。

entries.definition: A large ecological region defined by climate and vegetation, such as a rainforest. The biosphere is the sum of all biomes.
entries.definitionCN: 由气候与植被界定的大尺度生态区域，如雨林；生物圈是所有生物群系的总和。

entries.definition: A community of organisms together with its physical environment. It can be as small as a pond and need not be global.
entries.definitionCN: 生物群落与其物理环境的整体；可以小到一个池塘，不必是全球尺度。

entries.definition: The place where a particular species lives. It is species-specific, while the biosphere is the total living zone.
entries.definitionCN: 某一特定物种生活的地方；它针对物种，而生物圈是全部生命所在的区域。

entries.definition: The gaseous envelope of a planet. It is one of the spheres that exchange matter with the biosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 行星的气体包层；它是与生物圈交换物质的圈层之一。

entries.definition: The global system of life together with its environment. It overlaps with biosphere but stresses the system rather than the layer.
entries.definitionCN: 全球生命与其环境的整体系统；与 biosphere 重叠，但强调系统而非圈层。

entries.definition: All the living things of a region or of Earth. It names the organisms, not the zone they occupy.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区或地球上的全部生物；它命名生物本身，而不是它们占据的区域。

entries.definition: The Earth or a realm of activity. It is far vaguer than biosphere, which is a defined layer of the planet.
entries.definitionCN: 地球或某个活动领域；比 biosphere 模糊得多，后者是行星上一个被界定的圈层。

entries.definition: The conditions surrounding an organism. It can exclude the organisms themselves, unlike biosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕生物的条件；与 biosphere 不同，它可以把生物本身排除在外。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + sphere 'ball': the layer of life on the ball of Earth.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ sphere「球」：地球这个球上的生命之层。

normal.en: The family runs biology, biota, biome, biosphere, biospheric, antibiotic, biography.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 biology、biota、biome、biosphere、biospheric、antibiotic、biography。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: biosphere reserve, biosphere integrity, terrestrial biosphere, marine biosphere.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：生物圈保护区、生物圈完整性、陆地生物圈、海洋生物圈。

normal.en: The spheres run atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere.
normal.cn: 各圈层为：大气圈、水圈、岩石圈、生物圈。

normal.en: The biosphere is the whole; a biome is one large region inside it.
normal.cn: 生物圈是整体，生物群系是其中一个大的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a blue marble with a green film so thin that a fingernail could scrape it off.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗蓝色弹珠，上面覆着一层薄到指甲就能刮掉的绿膜。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed glass ball where the plants must remake the air for the animals.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密封玻璃球，里面的植物必须为动物重新制造空气。

abstract.en: Picture a planet where the rocks breathe because the living layer taught them to.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗岩石也会呼吸的行星，因为生命层教会了它。

examples.en: Carbon moves between the biosphere and the atmosphere constantly.
examples.cn: 碳在生物圈与大气之间不断移动。

examples.en: The biosphere reserve protects both the forest and the village inside it.
examples.cn: 生物圈保护区既保护森林，也保护其中的村庄。

examples.en: No sealed biosphere has yet supported people for many years.
examples.cn: 至今还没有封闭生物圈能多年维持人的生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: bio（生命）+ sphere（球、圈）→ 生命之球 → 生物圈

root: 希腊 bios「生命」+ sphaira「球、球体」→ 1875 年 Eduard Suess 造 Biosphere → 英语 biosphere。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all treat life as a layer or a system: Earth's living zone, another planet's life, an ecological component, a sealed experiment, a planetary actor, a support system, a protected area and a field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把生命视为一个圈层或一个系统：地球的生命区、其他行星的生命、生态组分、封闭实验、行星行动者、支持系统、保护区与研究领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blue planet wrapped in a green film thinner than an apple's skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗蓝色行星裹着比苹果皮还薄的绿色膜。

chain: ONE BOX IN THE EARTH SYSTEM

branches.en: THE LAYER: a thin zone of life, treated as one component of the planet.
branches.cn: 圈层：薄薄的生命带，被当作行星的一个组分。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS: the word detaches from Earth and names any planet's living layer.
branches.cn: 其他世界：该词脱离地球，指任何行星的生命层。

branches.en: THE SEALED MODEL: a miniature biosphere tests whether life can recycle its own conditions.
branches.cn: 封闭模型：微型生物圈检验生命能否循环维持自身条件。

branches.en: LIFE AS ACTOR: the biosphere exchanges matter with air and water and keeps conditions livable.
branches.cn: 生命作为行动者：生物圈与空气、水交换物质，并维持条件宜居。

branches.en: NAMES ON MAPS AND IN JOURNALS: the same word became a protected area and a scientific field.
branches.cn: 地图与期刊上的名字：同一个词变成了保护区与科学领域。

intro.en: Biosphere is a scientific compound of two Greek roots: life and ball. It was made in the nineteenth century and needs no further affix to name its object.
intro.cn: biosphere 是由两个希腊词根构成的科学复合词：生命与球。它于十九世纪造成，命名其对象时不再需要别的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios gives biology, biota, biosphere and antibiotic; Greek sphaira, through Latin sphaera, gives sphere, spherical, atmosphere and hydrosphere. Biosphere sits where the two families meet.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 bios 给出 biology、biota、biosphere、antibiotic；希腊 sphaira 经拉丁 sphaera 给出 sphere、spherical、atmosphere、hydrosphere。biosphere 正处在两个词族的交会处。

items.meaning: the living layer of a planet
items.example: The biosphere absorbs a large share of our carbon emissions.
items.exampleCN: 生物圈吸收了我们排放的很大一部分碳。

items.example: Biospheric models link life to climate.
items.exampleCN: 生物圈模型把生命与气候联系起来。

items.example: Biology split into many subfields in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 生物学在二十世纪分成许多子领域。

items.meaning: all living things of a region
items.example: The island's biota includes no large mammals.
items.exampleCN: 该岛的生物区系中没有大型哺乳动物。

items.example: The tundra biome has a short growing season.
items.exampleCN: 苔原生物群系的生长季很短。

items.example: The antibiotic blocks cell wall growth.
items.exampleCN: 该抗生素阻断细胞壁的生成。

items.meaning: a ball; a field of activity
items.example: The earth is not a perfect sphere.
items.exampleCN: 地球并不是完美的球体。

items.meaning: the gas envelope of a planet

scene: 白皮树在风里沙沙作响，落叶铺满小径。The old schoolmaster kept a birch in the closet.

senses.title: A slender tree with pale bark
senses.definition: a tree of cold regions with smooth pale bark and thin branches
senses.definitionCN: 寒带树种，树皮光滑色浅，枝条纤细
senses.example: The old schoolmaster kept a birch in the closet.
senses.exampleCN: 老校长在柜子里备着一束桦条。
senses.why: The Old English name for the tree, related to an ancient root for bright, for its shining bark.
senses.whyCN: 古英语树名，或与表示「明亮」的古词根相关，指其树皮发亮。

senses.title: The wood of the birch
senses.definition: the hard pale wood of the birch tree
senses.definitionCN: 桦树的浅色硬木
senses.example: The cabinet was made of solid birch.
senses.exampleCN: 这口柜子用整块桦木制成。
senses.why: Tree-names pass easily to their timber.
senses.whyCN: 树名常转指其木材。

senses.title: A bundle of birch twigs for flogging
senses.definition: a bunch of birch twigs formerly used to whip offenders
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用桦枝扎成、用于抽打犯错者的笞具
senses.example: Boys feared the birch more than detention.

definition_zh: n. 小餐馆，小酒馆（供应简单家常菜）；这类小馆的家常做法
definition_en: a small informal restaurant serving simple food; the plain home-style cooking associated with such places

senses.title: A small informal restaurant
senses.titleCN: 供应简单饭菜的小餐馆

senses.definitionCN: 桌椅朴素、供应简单菜式与饮品的小餐馆
senses.example: We ate at a bistro near the station, standing room only.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近的小馆吃饭，只能站着。
senses.why: The word came into French from the language of soldiers and travellers, and it names a place that feeds people quickly and plainly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由士兵与旅人的语言进入法语，指能让人快速、简单地吃饱的地方。

senses.title: The plain style of such cooking
senses.definition: the simple, hearty cooking typical of small neighbourhood restaurants
senses.definitionCN: 小社区餐馆典型的简单实在的烹饪风格

senses.why: What a place serves becomes a style, so the noun turns into the name of a way of cooking.

intro.en: Bistro is French, and its origin is disputed; the popular Russian story has no firm evidence.

items.cn: 法语 bistro 最初指巴黎的小酒馆。

items.en: A folk tale says Russian soldiers shouted a word meaning quickly.
items.cn: 民间传说称俄国士兵喊过一个意为「快」的词。

items.en: Linguists find no written record to support that story.
items.cn: 语言学家找不到支持该传说的书面记录。

items.en: The word spreads with the small eating houses of the city.
items.cn: 这个词随巴黎的小饭馆一同传开。

items.en: English borrows bistro for a modest, stylish restaurant.
items.cn: 英语借入 bistro，指朴素而有格调的小餐馆。

items.en: Bistro now also labels a plain style of cooking.
items.cn: 现代 bistro 也用来标指一种朴素的家常做法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short French shape with b; the near-meaning group ranks eating places by size and formality.
note.cn: 形近组与 bistro 同是带 b 的短小法语形；近义组按规模与正式程度排列餐饮场所。

senses.title: Every two weeks

definition_zh: 怪诞的；离奇的；奇异的
definition_en: very strange or unusual, often strikingly so
core_image: 戴着高帽的火烈鸟走进地铁车厢
scene: 剪彩那天，市长居然穿着戏服致辞。The carnival featured bizarre costumes and music.
sceneCN: 这里 bizarre 是「怪诞的、奇异的」（第 1 个义项：奇特到令人侧目）；句意是狂欢节上的服饰和音乐怪诞夺目。

derivatives.zh: bizarre 加 -ly，义为「怪异地；离奇地」

senses.title: Strangely outlandish
senses.definition: very strange in appearance, manner, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 外貌、举止或想法上极为怪异
senses.example: The carnival featured bizarre costumes and music.
senses.exampleCN: 狂欢节上的服饰和音乐怪诞夺目。
senses.why: The word came through Spanish and Italian bizarro, once meaning brave or odd.
senses.whyCN: 该词经西班牙语与意大利语 bizarro 传入，该词曾兼指勇武与古怪。

senses.title: Unbelievably odd in events
senses.definition: so strange that it seems hardly credible
senses.definitionCN: 怪异到几乎令人难以置信
senses.example: Their meeting was a bizarre coincidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的相遇是一场离奇的巧合。
senses.why: Events, like costumes, can be dressed in strangeness.
senses.whyCN: 事件如衣装，也可披上怪诞外衣。

senses.title: Grotesque in art or style
senses.definition: consciously strange and distorted in artistic design
senses.definitionCN: 艺术设计中刻意求怪的变形与奇诡
senses.example: The painter loved bizarre angles and colours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家偏爱怪异的角度与色彩。
senses.why: Art exaggerates to startle, and bizarre names the effect.
senses.whyCN: 艺术以夸张惊人，bizarre 正名其效。

senses.title: Erratic or unsettling in behaviour
senses.definition: of conduct so odd that it unsettles others
senses.definitionCN: 举止怪异到令他人不安
senses.example: His bizarre outbursts worried his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他反常的暴怒让朋友们担忧。
senses.why: Conduct off all maps reads as bizarre.
senses.whyCN: 越出一切常规的举止即显怪诞。

senses.title: Fantastical in invention
senses.definition: wildly imaginative to the point of strangeness
senses.definitionCN: 想象力狂放到近乎怪异
senses.example: The novel is set in a bizarre underwater city.
senses.exampleCN: 小说虚构了一座怪诞的海底之城。
senses.why: Invention without limits turns bizarre.
senses.whyCN: 无边际的想象终成怪诞。

senses.title: Incongruous mixtures
senses.definition: odd because of strangely matched parts
senses.definitionCN: 因搭配离奇而显得怪异
senses.example: It was a bizarre mix of opera and skateboarding.
senses.exampleCN: 那是歌剧与滑板的怪异混搭。
senses.why: Wrong partners make the whole picture strange.
senses.whyCN: 错位的组合令整体画面失谐。

senses.title: Funny-strange in humour
senses.definition: odd in a way that provokes laughter
senses.definitionCN: 以怪异引人发笑
senses.example: The sketch's bizarre logic kept the audience laughing.
senses.exampleCN: 小品荒诞的逻辑让观众笑个不停。
senses.why: Strangeness tipped into comedy is still bizarre.
senses.whyCN: 怪异滑向喜剧时仍是 bizarre。

senses.title: Reporting the surreal in news
senses.definition: describing real events that feel surreal
senses.definitionCN: 形容真实却如梦境的新闻事件
senses.example: Reporters called the traffic jam a bizarre saga.
senses.exampleCN: 记者把那场大堵车称为离奇长剧。
senses.why: When reality outdoes fiction, bizarre marks the gap.
senses.whyCN: 现实胜过虚构之际，bizarre 标记落差。

intro.en: Bizarre traveled from Italian and Spanish bizarro, brave and odd.

items.cn: 意大利语 bizarro 意为「勇猛」，后转指「古怪、奇幻」。

items.en: bizarre settled as strange, fantastic.
items.cn: 法语 bizarre 定型为「怪异、离奇」。

items.en: English borrowed the French sense in the 17th century.

definition_zh: 清淡的；乏味的；温和的；平淡无奇的
definition_en: lacking strong flavour, or lacking excitement and strong character
core_image: 一碗没放盐的白粥
scene: 食客尝了一口汤，默默地又撒了半勺盐。The soup was too bland for my taste.
sceneCN: 这里 bland 是「清淡无味的」（第 1 个义项：食物缺少味道）；句意是这汤太淡，不合我的口味。

derivatives.zh: bland 加 -ly，义为「温和地；乏味地」
bland 加 -ness，义为「平淡；温和无奇」
同源动词，义为「讨好；奉承」

senses.title: Lacking strong flavour
senses.definition: food that has little or no strong taste
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有浓烈味道的食物
senses.example: The soup was too bland for my taste.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤太淡，不合我的口味。
senses.why: Flavour is a kind of heat or force, and bland names its absence.
senses.whyCN: 味道本是一种力道，bland 标记的正是力道的缺席。

senses.title: Gentle and soothing, of remedies
senses.definition: of medicine or soap, mild and not irritating
senses.definitionCN: 药物或清洁用品性质温和、不刺激
senses.example: Wash the rash with bland soap and water.
senses.exampleCN: 用温和的肥皂和清水清洗皮疹。
senses.why: What carries no force cannot sting, so mild things keep the bland name.
senses.whyCN: 不带力道之物不会刺痛，温和之物因而沿用此名。

senses.title: Showing no strong emotion
senses.definition: of a face or manner, calm and showing no strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 面容或态度平和、不见强烈情绪
senses.example: He gave a bland smile and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他淡淡一笑，换了个话题。
senses.why: A face without expression is like food without salt: nothing registers.
senses.whyCN: 没有表情的脸如无盐的菜：什么都尝不出来。

senses.title: Dull and uninteresting
senses.definition: so lacking in interest or excitement that it bores
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味或刺激到令人厌倦
senses.example: The film's bland plot forgot to thrill anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 影片平淡的情节没能让任何人兴奋。
senses.why: Excitement is flavour for the mind, and its absence earns the same word.
senses.whyCN: 刺激之于头脑如味道之于舌头，缺席时共用其名。

senses.title: Deliberately neutral in speech
senses.definition: of statements, carefully neutral so as to offend no one
senses.definitionCN: 言辞刻意中性，避免冒犯任何人
senses.example: The statement was bland enough to mean nothing at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这份声明四平八稳到毫无实义。
senses.why: Removing all edge from words leaves only blandness, like watered soup.
senses.whyCN: 把言辞的锋芒全部去掉，只剩清汤寡水般的平淡。

senses.title: Lacking distinctive character
senses.definition: of places or designs, unremarkable and without identity
senses.definitionCN: 场所或设计毫无辨识度、千篇一律
senses.example: Airport hotels everywhere look bland and identical.
senses.exampleCN: 各地的机场酒店看上去千篇一律、毫无特色。
senses.why: Character is the spice of a place; strip it and the place reads as bland.
senses.whyCN: 特色是地方之香料，剥去之后便只剩平淡。

senses.title: Smooth-mannered to the point of insincerity
senses.definition: polite and smooth in a way that seems hollow
senses.definitionCN: 客气圆滑却显得空洞无诚
senses.example: The salesman's bland charm wore thin fast.
senses.exampleCN: 推销员那副圆滑的殷勤很快就让人腻烦。
senses.why: Charm without conviction tastes as empty as a spiceless dish.
senses.whyCN: 没有诚意的魅力，如没有香料的菜一样空乏。

senses.title: Of weather or light, mild and unvarying
senses.definition: of climate or light, mild and without sharp change
senses.definitionCN: 气候或光线温和且少有剧烈变化
senses.example: The coast enjoys a bland climate all year.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸全年气候温和宜人。
senses.why: Weather without sting or storm keeps the mild, bland name.
senses.whyCN: 不冷不烈、无风无暴的天气沿用「温和」之名。

intro.en: Bland comes from Latin blandus, soft-tongued and flattering.
intro.cn: bland 来自拉丁语 blandus，本义「言辞温柔的、谄媚的」。

items.cn: 一般认为出自表示「缓慢、轻柔」之意的词根的鼻化形式，来源不确定。

items.en: blandus meant caressing, flattering, mild in speech.
items.cn: 拉丁语 blandus 意为「抚慰的、谄媚的、言辞温和的」。

items.en: blando kept the soft, gentle sense.
items.cn: 意大利语 blando 保留「柔软、温和」之义。

items.en: blando likewise means soft.
items.cn: 西班牙语 blando 同样意为「柔软的」。

items.en: English took blandus for smooth and flattering speech, then for mildness of every kind.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪借入，先指言辞圆滑讨巧，后扩指各类温和无味。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bland- root; the near-meaning group gathers mild, flavourless words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bland- 词根；近义组汇集温和无味类词。

definition_en: a thick cover used to keep warm in bed
core_image: 沙发上叠得厚厚的毛毯
scene: 沙发上叠着一条厚厚的毛毯。She pulled the blanket up to her chin.
sceneCN: 这里 blanket 是「毯子」（第 1 个义项：保暖的厚覆盖物）；句意是她把毯子拉到下巴。

senses.title: A thick warm bed cover
senses.definition: a thick cover made of wool or similar material for warmth
senses.definitionCN: 用羊毛或类似材料制成、用于保暖的厚覆盖物
senses.example: She pulled the blanket up to her chin.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毯子拉到下巴。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, a cloth spread over a sleeper.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，一块盖在睡觉者身上的布。

senses.title: A thick covering layer
senses.definition: a thick layer that covers something completely

senses.whyCN: 积雪像布一样铺在地上，覆盖物这个词就扩展开来。

senses.title: Applying to everything

senses.example: The city issued a blanket ban on smoking.
